    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By OLLIE LEWIS, SPORTS DIGITAL EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.
    • Published: 05:58 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:41 EST, 23 November 2026.
    • Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the fresh manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By OLLIE LEWIS, SPORTS DIGITAL EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 05:58 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:41 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the fresh manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.

    Pochettino, who replaced Michael Carrick last week, was served a sobering reality check at the hands of United's fierce rivals Liverpool, with the Red Devils on the receiving end of a 4-0 trouncing on Merseyside.

    The Argentine bemoaned the impact of what he described as a harsh red card against defender Leny Yoro in the opening eight minutes of the contest, but admitted he has plenty to do to turn things around - with United stuck in 19th in the Premier League table.

    And Pochettino had his players check in for training early on Monday morning, with a downcast Bruno Fernandes and his team-mates spotted arriving at around 8.30am - roughly an hour earlier than under Carrick.

    Under Carrick's stewardship, players were given the day after a game off, and it remains to be seen whether Pochettino will do away with that approach in favour of a recovery day at the club's training ground - a similar approach to that taken by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

    Man United stars were ordered back into training on Monday after their trouncing at Anfield.

    Matthijs de Ligt cut a contemplative figure as he drove through the gates at Carrington.

    Director of football Jason Wilcox continues to have questions to answer after Man United were unable to elevate themselves out of the relegation zone.

    News also came on Monday that Man United are appealing to the FA over Yoro’s controversial red card.

    Sources indicate that yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free kick as 10-man United were thrashed 4-0.

    However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

    The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

    In September, Pro Ref boss Howard Webb apologised to United when Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand after VAR incorrectly ruled that teammate Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play as he tried to head the ball in an offside position.

    Last season, Webb acknowledged that the match officials got it wrong when they decided not to send off Brentford captain Nathan Collins for hauling back Bryan Mbeumo inside the box as United lost 3-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium.

    Newly introduced United head coach Pochettino blamed Yoro’s red card for the heavy defeat in his first game in charge, and was unhappy that Barrott took no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area moments earlier.

    According to recent reports, 'So painful, so disappointed,' mentioned the Argentine. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

    In a recent development, 'It's clear that after eight minutes the proposal was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

    Industry observers note that 'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

    'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

    'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

    Industry observers note that 'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

    'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

    But more critical were former Red Devils Roy Keane and Gary Neville, both of whom were pushed to extremes assessing the match after the final whistle.

    Lisandro Martinez was among the Man United defenders that Gary Neville did not feel were up to the task at Anfield.

    But incoming manager Pochettino was keen to place the majority of blame on the harsh red card doled out to Leny Yoro.

    Neville was driven to slapping his face in the Sky Sports studio to demonstrate Man United's defenders' lack of hunger and poise.

    'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', he mentioned before pointing to his head.

    'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

    Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

    The Overlap broadcaster slapped himself a number of times while repeating 'wake up!' and adding: 'You play for Man United'.

    Keane was pushed to the brink of swearing in his snap description of the team's performance, adding that he thought Neville's verdict - that the 4-0 scoreline might have been worse under the circumstances - took players off the hook.

    Sources indicate that 'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane remarked immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

    Industry observers note that 'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

    According to recent reports, '(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

    'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

    'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

    'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Newly introduced York Mets landed the offseason's best free agent and one of the game's top pitchers Sunday evening. The Mets and two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal have agreed to a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. The contract obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee (Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million) and average annual value (Max Scherzer's and Justin Verlander's $43.3 million). A 1-of-1 contract for a 1-of-1 pitcher.

    Latest York's offseason work is not complete, however. It's not close to complete, really. The Mets went 74-88 and disappointed every which way this past season. There are still roster needs to address. Here's what's left for the Mets to do this offseason following the Skubal signing.

    It has been revealed that yes, the Mets still need another starter even after signing Skubal. They have an excellent 1-2-3 punch. The depth behind that top three is not great, however. Here is New York's updated rotation depth chart:.

    Manaea and Senga both pitched so poorly this past season that they were demoted to the bullpen. They shouldn't be counted on as anything more than emergency options at this point in their careers. Thornton had some moments this summer and Tong is not too far removed from being a top prospect, but yeah, the Mets need another starter. Clearly.

    Recent findings suggest that after landing Skubal, I suspect the Mets will aim lower than the second tier of free agent starters (Michael King, Freddy Peralta, Trevor Rogers, etc.) to fill out their rotation. A Clay Holmes reunion would make some sense. Others in that class of veterans make sense too. Think Kevin Gausman, Shota Imanaga, Casey Mize, pitchers like that.

    Year 1 post-Pete Alonso at first base went worse than anyone could have expected. Jorge Polanco barely played and was terrible when he did play. Jared Young was fine and owner Steve Cohen isn't running near-record payrolls for fine. Alonso led all first basemen with 5.0 WAR for the Orioles. The Mets finished dead last at the position with -0.8 WAR. Yeesh.

    Here are the best available free agent first basemen by FanGraphs projected 2027 WAR:.

    In a recent development, it ain't great. I think the projections on France, who had an excellent season in 2026, are a bit low, but the fact of the matter is he's only had one year in line with the kind of contract he's likely to sign. Perhaps there's a Luis García Jr. trade to be made with the crosstown rival Upcoming York Yankees? García's a clunky fit for the Yankees and might be most useful as a trade chip.

    The good news is it won't be hard for the Mets to improve at first base. Getting even an average first baseman would represent an enormous upgrade. Now the Mets just have to go out and find that average (or, preferably, better than average) first baseman and improve their lineup. This might be the single biggest item remaining on their offseason to-do list.

    The Mets traded away several relievers at the deadline this summer (A.J. Minter, Brooks Raley, Luke Weaver, etc.), which allowed them to audition a few young pitchers down the stretch. Left-hander Nate Lavender in particular stood out and cemented his place in the 2027 bullpen. The bullpen pecking order currently looks something like this:.

    According to recent reports, williams was at best inconsistent during his first season with the Mets. Another late-inning reliever to share the high-leverage load (someone to replace Weaver, basically) seems essential. You don't want to pay Skubal all that money only to have the bullpen blow his starts, you know? President of baseball operations David Stearns is adept at building bullpens on the cheap. Spending money is OK too.

    Assuming the Mets don't go to the top of the market for Adrian Morejon, the best available free agent relievers are battle-tested veterans like Bryan Abreu, JoJo Romero, and Alex Vesia. Abreu is an excellent buy-low candidate after his rocky first half. There is no such thing as too many good relievers. The Mets should continue adding to their bullpen this winter.

    The case can be made that Skubal's contract is only the second smartest contract the Mets gave out this weekend. They agreed to an eight-year, $95 million contract with a ninth-year club option with center fielder A.J. Ewing on Saturday. The deal buys out his six years of team control and two free agent years with an option for a third. That's a nifty piece of business.

    Sources indicate that I would expect the Mets to pursue extensions with McLean and outfielder Carson Benge next, if they haven't already. McLean and Benge both had terrific first full seasons in the big leagues and look like keepers, like players who can be centerpieces for a World Series contender rather than just tag along for the ride. Locking up McLean and/or Benge would be fantastic work.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    ARLINGTON, Texas -- AT&T Stadium went from a full-throated roar to so deathly quiet that one could hear a scoop of cranberry sauce drop with two seconds remaining on the clock on Thanksgiving Day.

    It has been revealed that when Philadelphia Eagles kicker Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal sailed through the uprights to complete a 21-point comeback, the largest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history, the sensation Dallas Cowboys owner/general manager Jerry Jones felt when the stadium scoreboard read "Eagles 39, Cowboys 38" was numb. Nothingness. Emptiness. "Numbing" was the feeling Jones kept going back to outside the locker room postgame.

    "The word is numbing. Numbing at the end," Jones said postgame. "I didn't expect to be having this kind of conversation with you guys about 10 minutes left in that game.".

    Sources indicate that the Cowboys (5-7) desperately needed a win on Thanksgiving to get back to .500 and maintain a spot nipping at the heels of the NFC East-leading Fresh York Giants (6-3-1). They were well on their way to doing so after quarterback Dak Prescott's 12-yard scoring strike out to running back Javonte Williams put Dallas on top 28-10 at halftime. Following kicker Brandon Aubrey draining a 59-yard field goal with 3:35 left in the third quarter, the Cowboys' lead ballooned to 21.

    It has been revealed that then, everything came crashing down. Eagles fill-in quarterback Joe Milton, one of Dallas' backup quarterbacks up until October when the Eagles signed him off of the Dallas practice squad, carved the Cowboys up like Thanksgiving turkey, throwing for 331 yards and an interception on 21-of-31 passing with a 15-yard rushing touchdown. He hit on touchdown passes of 50 yards and 45 yards to wide receiver DeVonta Smith (200 yards receiving and two touchdowns on 11 catches) as well as on a 24-yarder to rookie first-round pick wide receiver Makai Lemon. No defense could have possessed a greater understanding of an opposing quarterback's tendencies than Milton, someone they worked against every day in practice as their scout team quarterback up until just over a month ago.

    Sources indicate that oh, and this happened against an Eagles team (4-7) that is a husk of the squad that steamrolled the entire league en route to a Super Bowl title at the end of the 2024 season. They entered Thanksgiving Thursday without Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) and All-Pro linebacker Zack Baun (back). They also lost running back Saquon Barkley (stinger), cornerback Cooper DeJean (concussion) and tight end Dallas Goedert (shoulder) during the game. Six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired in-season a number of weeks ago. It didn't matter.

    It has been revealed that aubrey, who signed a four-year, $28 million extension with $20 million guaranteed that made him the NFL's highest-paid kicker this past offseason, missed a 40-yard field goal that would have put the Cowboys up 11 with 3:42 left to play. A blocked punt returned for a touchdown made the Eagles believe they could come back with the margin trimmed down to seven, with 13:46 left to play.

    After the special teams' shakiness, coach Brian Schottenheimer decided to put the football in Prescott's hands on a game-clinching fourth-and-1 at the Eagles' 39 with 55 seconds remaining. However, Prescott got sacked for a nine-yard loss, and the Eagles' next drive ended with Elliott's game-winner with two seconds left on the clock.

    Industry observers note that prescott was left stunned and agreed with Jones that numb was an appropriate way to describe his postgame emotions. The light was clearly gone from the ever-resilient and optimistic quarterback's eyes at his postgame press conference. After all, his 2026 Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to average over 30 points per game (31.3 points per game, the second most in the NFL this season) and have a losing record through 12 games, according to CBS Sports Research.

    "Pretty stunning," Prescott noted. "[Numb is] a good description for how I'm feeling right now. Yeah, especially this soon after the game, understanding the plays left out there, the plays we could have made, should have made and the mistakes we had.".

    According to recent reports, perhaps the most deflating part of Dallas blowing a 14-plus-point lead at home against a team with a losing record is that this wasn't the Cowboys' first time doing so. Prior to November, Dallas was 202-0-1 when leading by that much in the fourth quarter at home in the 67-season existence of Cowboys football. Fast forward to Thanksgiving, and the Cowboys have lost twice this month in that situation against rebuilding teams with backup quarterbacks.

    Sources indicate that dallas allowed Gardner Minshew and the NFC West bottom-feeding Arizona Cardinals (3-8) to dig out of a 24-10 hole and win 33-30 in overtime. That was the worst loss of the 2026 season until Thursday. The Cowboys don't play again for 11 more days when they suit up again in Seattle against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks (6-4) on "Monday Night Football." This is one of the rare cases where having more time to process the grief from a letdown loss might be a bad thing.

    "Hopefully it helps, but it's definitely going to sting during it and particularly these next couple of days," Prescott mentioned of the 11-day layoff. "But as we get back into the building, we can't allow this to hold us back.".

    According to recent reports, the problem for Dallas is that the Cardinals and Eagles home losses are hardly the only soul-crushing defeats of the year. Here's a quick rundown if you've lost count.

    Days after the 49ers loss, Schottenheimer stripped first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of defensive play-calling duties while still keeping him on the coaching staff. He gave defensive play-calling to Parker's mentor Mike Pettine, who was recently hired on staff out of retirement as a senior defensive assistant.

    According to recent reports, the hits just keep on coming, and this latest one prevented Dallas from getting back to .500 at 6-6 ahead of playing the NFL's second-toughest remaining strength of schedule. Their final five opponents have a combined winning percentage of .608, so this loss essentially erased all hope for an NFC East division title run.

    "The message shouldn't have to motivate you, shouldn't have to inspire," Prescott noted about how to keep the team together. "It shouldn't be the reason that you go win, or the message wasn't good enough, and it's the reason that we lost. So there's got to be a sense of accountability that doesn't fall on the messenger.".

    * First team ever with two home losses in a season up 14-plus points in the fourth quarter, per CBS Sports Research.

    Dallas surrendered 22 fourth-quarter points on defense to an Eagles team that hadn't scored more than that amount in an entire game since Week 2, Philadelphia's last game before their seven-game losing streak ended in Week 11 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, which ended up imploding that franchise.

    Sources indicate that the Cowboys' 2026 season isn't officially over, but it might as well be. Games at the 2025 NFC finalists — the Seahawks (6-4) and Los Angeles Rams (7-4) — loom, as do matchups with the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3), the Giants (6-3-1) and the surging Washington Commanders (4-5-1). Dallas has too much scar tissue, both mentally and physically, to realistically get back into the NFC East race.

    It has been revealed that "I mean, it's a gut check for sure. Told the guys that," Schottenheimer said postgame. "Division football. That's what we talked about in the locker room.".

    Prescott remarked everyone from the top down in the Cowboys franchise needs to take some time off this weekend before hitting the ground running.

    "And [we have to] get back to it with more urgency and better than ever individually and collectively to give it our best chance," Prescott stated.

    According to recent reports, but are these battered and scarred Cowboys able to successfully respond and bounce back from yet another gut-wrenching loss? The face of the franchise quarterback who is tasked with being Mr. Perfect on and off the field in Dallas couldn't answer that question definitively.

    Prescott likely couldn't do so because, deep down, he already knows: The 2026 season will go down as another year of his prime wasted in another lost Cowboys campaign. That's why that numbing feeling is setting in for Jones and his Cowboys once again.

    #166315. Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1543 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books.
    • After battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history.
    • These Warriors have lost their last four by 109 points, and what makes it even more jarring is comparing them to the team that had won eight straight prior to Curry's injury.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books. So it's really saying something to start registering all-time marks of franchise ineptitude, which is precisely what the Warriors have done over the last week.

    After battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history. The only other time this has happened to a Warriors team was in February of 1998, a few months after Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo. The total margin of that four-game losing streak was 104 points.

    This current one is even worse. These Warriors have lost their last four by 109 points, and what makes it even more jarring is comparing them to the team that had won eight straight prior to Curry's injury. That 1997-98 team was trash all year, starting 1-14 and finishing with just 19 wins without ever winning more than three straight games.

    These Warriors, on the other hand, were starting to look like a legitimate playoff-caliber team. A cynic would say that run of victories came against a softer schedule than what they have faced of late, but that qualification doesn't hold much, if any, water. That eight-game run included wins over the Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat and an Orlando Magic team that has immediately gone on to win five of its last six.

    Perhaps the Warriors would have lost to the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs even with Curry. Hell, maybe they would've lost to the New Orleans Pelicans, Dallas Mavericks and Memphis Grizzlies, too. That feels unlikely, but who knows? Even with Curry, the Warriors aren't good enough to start checking off scheduled wins. But that's not the point.

    The point is how utterly incapable they have looked in losing these games. Not only have they lost each of these last four by at least 20 points, but they've also been held under 100 points in all of them. That's a combination of incompetence that stretches beyond a franchise mark. That hasn't happened to a single other team this century.

    Before we try to answer that, let's just agree upfront that Curry has little to no chance of actually winning what would be his third MVP. The Warriors almost certainly won't have a good enough record to put him in real contention. His across-the-board counting stats, even if he were to maintain his torrid early pace, are not going to match those of Luka Dončić or Victor Wembanyama.

    The only real chance would be if both of those guys, and likely a bunch of others, failed to meet the 65-game threshold, but the chances of Curry, who has already missed six games and isn't expected to be re-evaluated until around Thanksgiving, making it to 65 games himself already feel next to impossible. He may be past the maximum 17 games-missed mark before he even returns from this injury.

    Which is to say, what we're asking here is whether Curry, at 38 years old and in his 18th season, is still the most valuable player in the league (has he always been?), not whether he'll actually win the award, and the answer to that question, at least in its simplest form, could very well lie in his absence. Just look at this team without him.

    Eight-game win streak with Curry.

    Four-game losing streak without Curry.

    Admittedly, there's some cherry-picking in those numbers. Curry actually didn't play in one of the wins during that eight-game streak, and the Warriors still beat the Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with a 122.8 offensive rating behind 37 points from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

    We're also leaving out the aforementioned game against the Rockets on Nov. 11 in which Curry only played six minutes and the Warriors looked fine, or even good, in testing one of the best teams in the league to its limit. It also must be noted that Golden State lost its first three games of the season and looked every bit like the team many of us predicted would stink, all of which Curry played in.

    In a recent development, still, the general rule applies. The Warriors go as Curry goes. That was true even in the golden years when the on/off splits, even with the likes of Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson still out there, always pointed to Curry as the clear MVP.

    "If I didn't have Steph, I would've been like every other NBA coach and lasted a few years [with the Warriors] and then gone and coached somewhere else," Steve Kerr has said, openly admitting that Curry, and Curry alone, has been the difference between a journeyman coaching career and a Hall-of-Fame one.

    It has been revealed that he's not lying. Have a look at the numbers.

    According to recent reports, even if you want to remove the 2019-20 season from the equation, when Durant had defected, Thompson missed the whole year and Curry only played in five games, Kerr is still a below-.500 coach at 74-96 without Curry in the lineup. This is a coach who has had all kinds of great players at his disposal over the years, and still it was always Curry in control of his and the organization's ultimate fate.

    It has been revealed that this is still the case for the Warriors, who continue to fall off a cliff without Curry. When he's been on the floor this year, they have registered a 59.6 eFG%, which would rank first in the league. When he's off, they fall to 49.1%, which would rank last.

    Even the defensive decline we see in Curry's on/off splits can largely be tied back to his offense. Without him, the Warriors are unable to create the same shots and, when their newly introduced brand of shots miss far more often, they end up defending in transition on almost 3% more possessions. That's a massive deal. It's meant almost five more points per game surrendered to fast breaks over this stretch.

    In a recent development, the Warriors have produced an average offensive rating of 103.8 in games Curry hasn't played this year, which would rank as the second-worst mark in the league. All told, they are 26.3 points per 100 possessions better in Curry's minutes this season, per Cleaning The Glass. By comparison, the Lakers drop by 25.5 points per 100 when Dončić sits. Wembanyama is in his own galaxy with this stat, representing a 37.8-point decline in San Antonio when he's off the floor.

    It's fair to say Wembanyama means as much to San Antonio's defense, where most of that decline happens, as Curry does to Golden State's offense, and certainly the Lakers falling off by as much as they do offensively, even with Austin Reaves as a legit secondary star, tells you everything you need to know about his impact. All of these guys are MVP players.

    Industry observers note that but only one, by subjective definition, can be the most valuable, and the simple truth is the Lakers and Spurs are outfitted with far more functional rosters independent of their respective superstars. In Golden State, there is just nowhere else to turn. Nobody to generate any kind of consistent offensive leverage. No gravity. No shot creation.

    After the Warriors took that 38-point beating against the Spurs without Curry, the rookie Lendeborg, who had, in total unfairness, been saddled with filling Curry's go-to-scorer shoes, noted "it felt helpless out there," and that is exactly what it has looked like since the Curry variable was removed from Golden State's equation.

    To be fair, the absence of a player is an imperfect lens through which to view value for a bunch of contextual reasons, not the least of which is how a team like Golden State is designed to play -- a specific, Curry-centric ecosystem not particularly amenable to abrupt adjustments. These players are not as bad as they have looked without Curry over these last four games.

    But by the same token, they aren't close to as good as they looked with Curry, either. I always laugh when my dad calls me saying things like, "This Pat Spencer guy can play!" Everyone looks like they can play next to Curry. And then he goes away and suddenly you're wondering how the hell this guy made the Washington Generals look like one of the best teams in the league. Is he some kind of miracle worker?

    According to recent reports, in a basketball sense, that's not far off. Curry's individual production is already virtually unmatched, but it's his exponential powers, his ability to compound the returns of those around him, that set him apart. It's early, yes. Perhaps the Warriors will figure things out the longer Curry is away. Probably not. But maybe they at least can return to competitive functionality. Until then, however, it's pretty hard to not think Curry is the most valuable player in the league when you watch the Warriors play without him.

    #166313. Is Tarik Skubal a Hall of Famer? Where newly introduced Mets ace stands now and where he could end up

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (909 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Is Tarik Skubal a Hall of Famer? Where newly introduced Mets ace stands now and where he could end up

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Mets are signing Tarik Skubal to a monster deal: nine years and $450 million.
    • To be clear, Skubal is nowhere close to a Hall of Famer at this point, but that never stops people from throwing around titles like "future Hall of Famer." So, let's look ahead and guess a little bit and wonder if he is, in fact, a future Hall of Famer.
    • I'm inclined to say yeah, he's headed in that direction.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Mets are signing Tarik Skubal to a monster deal: nine years and $450 million. There's plenty to talk about with this deal, but a fun one for people like me -- especially here in the winter! -- would be glancing at his Hall of Fame case and how it's rounding into shape.

    To be clear, Skubal is nowhere close to a Hall of Famer at this point, but that never stops people from throwing around titles like "future Hall of Famer." So, let's look ahead and guess a little bit and wonder if he is, in fact, a future Hall of Famer.

    I'm inclined to say yeah, he's headed in that direction. There's a lot more compiling to be done, though.

    Industry observers note that in parts of seven seasons, Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA (138 ERA+), 1.02 WHIP and 1,975 strikeouts against 199 walks in 925 ⅓ innings. He's led the league in pitcher WAR twice, ERA twice, strikeouts once and WHIP once. The two-time All-Star is one of 23 pitchers in history to win multiple Cy Youngs. Only 11 pitchers have ever won three, so if he can grab another one, he'll be in Hall of Fame tech giant.

    In a recent development, some of us will give bonus points for great postseason numbers, and Skubal certainly has those. In three playoff seasons, he's 3-2 with a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts in 50 ⅔ innings.

    Still, we're awfully light here on workload and counting stats. Keep in mind that this is obviously a major work in progress and players aren't even eligible for the Hall of Fame until they've logged 10 years of service time. Skubal still has three more to go before this is even a real conversation.

    According to recent reports, at present, the most statistically similar pitchers are Corbin Burnes, Shane Bieber and a bunch of very good but not Hall-worthy guys. If we set the parameters to the most statistically similar pitchers through age 29, we'll find Kyle Hendricks, Adam Wainwright, Max Fried, Bieber and Burnes as the top five.

    Again, that doesn't sound like this pitcher is headed to the Hall of Fame.

    Keep in mind, though, that Skubal was a bit of a late bloomer and also had major surgery interrupt his rise. In these last three seasons, he's gone 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA and 655 strikeouts against only 95 walks in 546 innings. He's racked up 17.7 WAR in just three years. Another three like that and he'd be in the ballpark of 40 WAR heading into his age-33 season. Catfish Hunter (40.9) and Jack Morris (43.5) would be within reach.

    Sources indicate that it is incredibly difficult to predict how a pitcher will age, but with pitchers of Skubal's caliber, there's an excellent track record going into their late 30s. It's reasonable to believe Skubal will remain in his prime through age 35 or so.

    Sources indicate that let's say he averages roughly 6.0 WAR per season through age 35 and then averages, say, 2.5 (this is conservative) through the end of his contract. That would give him an additional 43.5 WAR. Add that to his current 22.7 and that gets him to 66.2 WAR through the end of this contract.

    No, WAR isn't the only stat that matters, but it's the easy catch-all number to eyeball the Hall of Fame standing.

    It has been revealed that in the range of 66.2, you'll find Hall of Famers Don Drysdale, John Smoltz, Carl Hubbell, Ed Walsh and Don Sutton, a nice smattering of many different eras of aces. A bit behind the number? Roy Halladay, Bob Feller, Juan Marichal, CC Sabathia and Early Wynn.

    According to recent reports, diving beyond WAR, again, Skubal's biggest résumé issue right now is the lack of compiling. With a strikeout artist, you'd like to see him reach 3,000, and he's barely a third of the way there.

    Using Bill James' "favorite toy," let's take a look at the career projection. The toy has Skubal finishing with 2,036 strikeouts and gives him a 0% chance to reach 3,000. Of course, it also notes that based on his age, he'll play for roughly 4.6 years. He just signed a nine-year deal. I'd be a bit more aggressive, but it isn't difficult to see him falling well short of 3,000 and maybe finishing around 2,500 or so.

    Recent findings suggest that still, given his age and service time, it seems like the best route for Skubal to get to the Hall of Fame would be as a peak candidate rather than a compiler. Another Cy Young or two would certainly help his case.

    If Skubal is in his prime for another five years, that would be seven or eight seasons as one of the best pitchers in baseball. That was enough for Sandy Koufax and Dizzy Dean. Félix Hernández is making good progress on getting in. Johan Santana, on the other hand, fell short.

    It remains an uphill battle because, well, it's incredibly difficult to make the Hall of Fame. It should be. It's the Hall of Fame!

    Recent findings suggest that without the context behind Skubal's recent surge, it doesn't look like he's headed to Cooperstown at all. He's good enough presently, though, to believe his next several years will put him on track.

    Again, my hunch is he'll end up a Hall of Famer.

    The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

    During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

    Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in upcoming manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

    Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

    Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

    Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

    Sources indicate that the game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

    Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

    It has been revealed that on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

    A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

    Sources indicate that leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a massive threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

    According to recent reports, flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

    Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

    According to recent reports, newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

    Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

    Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

    There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

    Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

    Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

    Newcastle get the game under way.

    It has been revealed that matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

    The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

    Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

    Newly introduced manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    “It’s a challenge, a major challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

    In a recent development, “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about upcoming signings.

    “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he remarked.

    “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle noted he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he stated.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the New York Mets have landed two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal, the offseason's top free agent, with a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million.
    • Every contract that long and that pricey carries risk and surely makes even the league's wealthiest owner a wee bit queasy.
    • "He's going to be great for the clubhouse ...
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the New York Mets have landed two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal, the offseason's top free agent, with a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. It far exceeds Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers, which was the previous record guarantee for a pitcher.

    Every contract that long and that pricey carries risk and surely makes even the league's wealthiest owner a wee bit queasy. After meeting with Skubal in California last week, though, Mets owner Steve Cohen came away convinced Skubal was his guy and that he would have no issues settling into his fresh environment.

    "He's going to be great for the clubhouse ... I don't have to worry about him pitching in New York," Cohen told the New York Post on Sunday, before the deal went official. "... He's an outstanding individual. He's bright. He's a student of the game. He's very impressive.".

    Industry observers note that the "can he handle New York?" thing tends to get overblown, but it is a real consideration. It's a different market with different demands and you never truly know how a player will handle it until he experiences it. I think Skubal will be more than fine in New York because I don't think you can be as successful as he's been without embracing the spotlight, but I don't know that for certain. No one does.

    Skubal has proven his bona fides on the biggest stages. He's been sensational in eight career postseason starts, pitching to a 2.13 ERA with 70 strikeouts in 50 ⅔ innings. All indications are that Skubal is a good teammate who fit in well with the Dodgers following his midseason trade from the Detroit Tigers.

    Now 30, Skubal posted a 2.72 ERA in 158 ⅔ innings around his NanoScope elbow procedure this past season. He leads all pitchers with 18.0 WAR over the last three years despite missing time with injury this year.

    The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. They were baseball's most disappointing team and signing Skubal is an enormous step toward making sure it doesn't happen again.

    Latest Update: In a Newly introduced York minute: Did Mikal Bridges just turn his season around with one shot?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (799 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mikal Bridges was always up against a nearly impossible standard in New York.
    • Bridges entered Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers averaging 7.5 points per game on putrid 40/30 shooting splits.
    • Industry observers note that he's been showing signs of life of late.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mikal Bridges was always up against a nearly impossible standard in New York. The Knicks sold everything but their soul to get him. He went from zero to hero over last year's championship run, then right back down to zero to start this season.

    Bridges entered Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers averaging 7.5 points per game on putrid 40/30 shooting splits. The familiar chatter was growing louder. Trade him. Or at least bench him. The Knicks entered Saturday having lost Bridges' minutes by a starter-worst five points per 100 possessions this season, per Databallr, and worse, they were +17.8 with him on the bench.

    Industry observers note that he's been showing signs of life of late. He went for 18 on 8-of-12 shooting against Indiana a week ago. He put up 17 on 7-of-11 in a win over the Raptors on Tuesday. The Knicks entered Saturday having won three straight and seven of their last nine.

    Make that four straight and eight of 10 as the Knicks stunned the Blazers 97-96 -- with Bridges turning his ever-extreme dial from zero all the way back up to hero with the shot that just may have turned his season around.

    Mike Breen doesn't bring out the double-bang often, but he did it on Saturday when Bridges took an inbound pass at the top of the key and, with the Knicks down two and 3.2 seconds on the clock, dribbled left and pulled up for the second buzzer-beater of his career (both of which have come against the Blazers).

    MIKAL BRIDGES HITS THE @TISSOT BUZZER-BEATER AS THE KNICKS WIN THEIR FOURTH STRAIGHT!🚨⏰ Everyone Gets 24 pic.twitter.com/UmtE1mOLRu.

    Sources indicate that this would've been a gut-punch loss for the Knicks, who were on the verge of fumbling a 23-point halftime lead. Instead, as it turned out, it couldn't have been scripted better. Bridges needed a moment like this.

    It has been revealed that mike Brown hasn't pulled him from the starting five, but he only played him for 17 minutes in two straight games less than two weeks ago, and Bridges' minutes, largely as a result of that stretch, are down to a career-low 26 a game, which is the same burn Landry Shamet gets. This Nov. 15 portrait of basketball depression just about summed up the state of Bridges' season at that point.

    Industry observers note that mikal Bridges and Jose Alvarado on the bench. 😕(h/t @IQfor3) pic.twitter.com/0UU7J4Fd2v.

    Fast forward to Saturday night, when Madison Square Garden came alive with more than 50 franchise legends in the building for Homecoming Night, and this is what you call a vibe shift.

    KNICKS LEGENDS REACT TO MIKAL BRIDGES' @TISSOT BUZZER-BEATER 🔥 https://t.co/drFU31goFh pic.twitter.com/8HxH5Avnww.

    "When, quote-unquote, you think he's struggling, he just keeps playing," Brown said of Bridges after Saturday's game. "He doesn't let anything impact him. ... He's not going to get too high, he's not going to get too low. He's been there and done that. So for him to have the ball in his hands at that point in the game, there's a lot of confidence not only coming from him but from his teammates and the staff.".

    In the interest of not totally overreacting to one shot, let's keep some perspective on this. Bridges only had 12 points vs. Portland. The Knicks still lost his 28 minutes by six points, the worst plus-minus of the night. But he made five of his eight shots and established a confident early rhythm.

    It has been revealed that bridges certainly hasn't been setting the world on fire, but for the most part he's been looking more like himself after a terrible start. The Knicks are now -49 for the season in Bridges' minutes, but they were -50 over the first three games, meaning he has been a net neutral since. That's nothing to celebrate, but it's not as bad as the prevailing perception.

    Now look at it the other way. The Knicks are +140 without Bridges on the court this season and, while there's no denying his contribution to that number with too many nothing offensive showings, understand that nearly half of it comes from two games (-24 against the Nets on Nov. 2 and -36 against the Bucks on Nov. 11).

    It has been revealed that this isn't to suggest Bridges has been anywhere close to good so far. It's just to say that small samples can look like bigger deals than they are, and generally speaking, he's been slowly coming around. Maybe he just needed one game, one shot, one moment to reroute his basketball brain back toward the space he left it in as a playoff hero. Maybe Saturday night was that moment. Like the great Don Henley said: In a Fresh York minute, everything can change.

    #166302. Predicting MLB's next mega contracts: Paul Skenes, Junior Caminero, James Wood and more in line to get paid

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1232 w)
    📖 Baca

    Predicting MLB's next mega contracts: Paul Skenes, Junior Caminero, James Wood and more in line to get paid

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1232 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that baseball has a latest highest-paid pitcher.
    • This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken.
    • Sources indicate that next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that baseball has a latest highest-paid pitcher. Sunday evening, the New York Mets landed two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal on a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. Yoshinobu Yamamoto previously held the record for the largest guarantee given to a pitcher at $325 million. Agent Scott Boras came in well above that with Skubal.

    This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken. Last offseason, Kyle Tucker set the average annual value record at $60 million. The offseason before that, Juan Soto set the record guarantee at $765 million. The offseason before that, Shohei Ohtani set records every which way with his heavily deferred 10-year, $700 million contract.

    Sources indicate that next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really? Add in the uncertainty created by the upcoming collective bargaining agreement and I don't think anyone can confidently say what the next few offseasons will look like, or when contract records will be set.

    It has been revealed that that won't stop us from speculating, however. Here now are 10 candidates to sign baseball's next mega contract, which we'll loosely define as a contract that makes us stop and say, "oh damn, that's a crazy deal." Sound good? Good. Let's get to it.

    Junior Caminero, Rays: Caminero and Hall of Famer Eddie Mathews are the only players in baseball history with two 40-homer seasons before their age-23 seasons. Power pays, always has and always will, and Caminero has power to spare. He is not scheduled to become a free agent until after 2030, when he'll still be only 28 years old. If he doesn't sign a contract extension that would no doubt set upcoming records for his service time level, Caminero will be in line for a Soto-esque deal come free agency, assuming of course he continues hitting home runs at this pace.

    According to recent reports, elly De La Cruz, Reds: De La Cruz reportedly rejected what would have been a franchise-record contract last offseason, beating Joey Votto's $225 million extension way back when. Still only 24, De La Cruz just turned in a sensational season, during which he went 30-30 and finished sixth among all players with 6.4 WAR. He is one of those guys who looks like he was put on this Earth for the sole purpose of playing baseball. De La Cruz is an all-around impact player, plus he's a high-energy player who plays with obvious joy. He is three years away from free agency and this is exactly the sort of skill set that gets a record contract.

    It has been revealed that paul Skenes, Pirates: You know you've set a high bar when a 4.2 WAR season is considered a disappointment and people spend the summer wondering what's wrong with you. The fact is, though, that Skenes did take a step back in 2026, and he'll have to return to his 2024-25 form to get a mega contract. Plus, he has to stay healthy, which is the unspoken "if" that exists with every pitcher. Skenes will turn only 25 in May and he's three years away from free agency. Even if 2026 proves to be his new normal, he'll get a massive payday as a free agent. And if Skenes rediscovers his 2024-25 form, Skubal's record will almost certainly fall.

    Gunnar Henderson, Orioles: A year or two ago Henderson, 25, would have been in the favorites category. He took a step back in 2025, however, and then another step back in 2026. To be sure, a 3.6-WAR season is still very good, but this is becoming a thing with top young Orioles hitters, no? Adley Rutschman regressed from legitimate star to pretty good. Now, Henderson seems to be on the same track. Henderson is only two years away from free agency. If his 2027-28 look more like 2023-24 than 2025-26, then forget it; he'll get a mega contract as a free agent at age 27. Star shortstops reliably get paid handsomely.

    Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers and Cam Schlittler, Yankees: This year's Cy Young winners are both five years away from free agency, which puts them at a clear disadvantage in the mega contract race. If they set any records, it will likely be for their service time level with an extension. Otherwise, we're talking about staying healthy and holding this level of performance through 2031 before Misiorowski and Schlittler sign mega deals. The Brewers aggressively lock up their best young players. Based on that, Misiorowski is more likely than Schlittler to sign a record extension for a pitcher this far away from free agency.

    James Wood, Nationals: There are very few hitters I would take over Wood for the next five years. He is terrific, with easy power and a discerning eye, and sneaky stolen base ability as well. Wood's outfield defense is not good and might keep him from getting a record contract. Then again, poor defense didn't keep Soto from signing the richest contract ever, and Wood is about the same caliber of hitter. He just turned 24 and he's four years away from free agency. Offense pays more than defense and Wood is going to hit 50 home runs one of these years. If it happens before free agency, all the better for his mega contract pursuit.

    According to recent reports, pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs: Why is the reigning National League MVP a long shot for a mega contract after a 10.6-WAR season? Because the Cubs wisely locked Crow-Armstrong up to a six-year, $115 million extension just before Opening Day. Furthermore, that contract doesn't begin until 2027. The Cubs have PCA locked up through 2032, his age-31 season. It will be difficult, then, for Crow-Armstrong to sign a record contract simply because free agents do not get paid as well when they're in their 30s. No one should reasonably expect 10-WAR seasons every year, but if PCA can continue at an All-Star pace through 2032, then maybe he'll get a record contract. It's not impossible. Just unlikely.

    Sources indicate that mason Miller, Padres: No, Miller will not approach Skubal's record, but he is already well-positioned to sign the richest reliever contract in baseball history. The current record is Edwin Díaz's five-year, $102 million deal with the Mets four years ago. I suppose Adrian Morejon, most recently Miller's teammate in San Diego, could break Díaz's record this offseason. Or maybe Jhoan Duran, who will be a free agent next offseason, breaks Díaz's record. As long as he stays healthy and remains this, Miller should break the reliever contract record, whatever it is, when the time comes. He is 28 and three years away from free agency.

    Jordan Walker, Cardinals: A bit of a reach, perhaps, but Walker finally arrived as a power-hitting force in 2026, plus he stole 22 bases as well. He's been around so long that it's easy to forget he's still only 24. Walker is on track to become a free agent after 2029, when he'll be only 27, and boy, 27-year-old power hitters are exactly the kind of players who get record contracts. Walker leveled up in 2026. If he levels up again in 2027 and as he gets close to his prime years, he's a sneaky good candidate to get a mega contract down the line.

    #166301. Dwight Howard admits he told Magic not to trade for Stephen Curry before he became 'one of the greatest'

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (965 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Dwight Howard admits he told Magic not to trade for Stephen Curry before he became 'one of the greatest'

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history.
    • The exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry.
    • There have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history. There were never serious rumors, for instance, about LeBron James or Michael Jordan getting traded. Magic Johnson and Kobe Bryant both issued public trade demands, but pulled back before a deal was consummated. Players like this, for the most part, don't make it to the rumor mill because nobody ever thinks they're seriously available.

    The exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry. Though the rumors all died once he hit his prime, there is a rich history of teams that nearly traded for the greatest shooter of all time before he became, well, the greatest shooter of all time. At least three notable deals were reportedly scuttled at the finish line:.

    There have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries. Of course, Curry differs from those contemporaries in one key way: he was not a sure thing. James came into the NBA as a preordained star. Anyone claiming they knew what Curry was going to become is almost certainly lying. There was quite a bit of doubt about him early in his career, and that doubt informs our latest entry into the Curry trade chronicles.

    According to recent reports, dwight Howard appeared on the AM Hoops Show on Saturday and shared something few would be eager to admit: he told his former team, the Orlando Magic, not to trade for Stephen Curry. "I wanted to play with Monta Ellis and the Magic wanted to get Steph. The Magic wanted to get Steph and I said no. I said no because I didn't know. I didn't know Steph Curry was going to be one of the greatest," Howard said, regretfully. Asked specifically if the Magic came to him with this, he confirmed. "At the time, Monta was the one who was playing all the minutes," he added.

    Sources indicate that howard did not offer a specific trade proposal or window of time when this could have happened, but two options come to mind. The first would be during the 2010-11 season, when Orlando revamped its team in mid-December by making two blockbuster deals that sent Vince Carter, Rashard Lewis, Marcin Gortat and Mickael Pietrus out while bringing back Gilbert Arenas, Hedo Turkoglu, Jason Richardson and Earl Clark. This would make sense as a period of roster transition, and Ellis was the league leader in minutes that season, averaging more than 40 per game across 80 appearances.

    Recent findings suggest that but Curry was no slouch that season when it came to availability either. He appeared in 74 games and averaged nearly 34 minutes. His availability didn't become a major concern until a year later, when ankle injuries limited him to just 26 games. At that point, his trade value would have been at its lowest, and Howard's leverage with the team would have been at its height. Howard had a player option for the 2012-13 season that he surprisingly exercised... even though the Magic didn't acquire Ellis. Orlando still wound up trading Howard to the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2012.

    Recent findings suggest that on paper, Curry was perhaps the perfect guard to pair with Howard at his peak. Of course, Curry was and remains the perfect player to pair with just about anyone, but Howard, specifically, tried and failed to mesh with two high-usage star guards in Kobe Bryant and James Harden. Curry's eagerness to play off of the ball would have allowed Howard more post-up possessions, a priority of his at the time even if such plays didn't represent great offense. The team could have run through Howard, but still benefitted enormously from the young Curry's presence before eventually shifting in Curry's direction as Howard aged out of his physical prime.

    Stan Van Gundy was a pioneer in the 3-point revolution, building a four-out lineup around Howard with players like Lewis and Turkoglu. It's tempting to think about what he could have done with a young Curry, especially since Van Gundy would miss another chance to coach him down the line, when he elected to take the Detroit Pistons job in 2014 rather than continuing to pursue Golden State's vacant position.

    But if there ever really was a window for someone to swoop in and steal Curry, it closed after that third, injury-plagued season. Curry broke out in the 2012-13 season by leading the Warriors back to the playoffs, made his first All-Star team a year later, and then a year after that, he won the first of his two MVP awards and four championships. From that point forward, Golden State had no reason to ever entertain the notion of trading Curry, and Howard, like the Suns, Hornets and Bucks, was left to wonder about what might have been.

    Sources indicate that ironically enough, Howard would get another chance to pair up with Curry in 2013, after Curry had proven himself as Golden State's lead guard. He was a free agent that offseason and met with the Warriors, but seemingly preferred Harden as his running mate, as he signed with the Houston Rockets. The Warriors turned around and used their cap flexibility to add dynasty mainstay Andre Iguodala, an essential part of a team that largely won without high-profile centers like Howard. With the benefit of hindsight, Howard might be one of the most important hidden figures in Golden State's rise to prominence. If he had any inkling of the sort of legend Curry was destined to become, the Warriors dynasty may never have happened.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026.
    • Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.
    • The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

    The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

    Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

    But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

    Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

    'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

    Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW.

    Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger).

    The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25.

    'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

    'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is notable to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'.

    Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

    Industry observers note that 'It's devastating,' noted Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

    Industry observers note that 'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just noted to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

    'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

    'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'.

    Industry observers note that holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

    Industry observers note that 'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

    Sources indicate that 'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'.

    Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

    Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

    Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

    'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway remarked on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

    In a recent development, 'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

    'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: MLB rumors: Mets' Tarik Skubal follow-up, where Blue Jays turn now, plus Yankees, Phillies, Red Sox, more

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets.
    • It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m.
    • It has been revealed that the Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the New York Post.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets. It is far and away the richest pitching contract in history, crushing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The Mets still have other things to address, including adding another starter, but they landed the winter's best free agent.

    It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the key offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Monday's hot stove happenings.

    It has been revealed that the Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the New York Post. Suter will make $3.75 million in 2026, and there's a $3.5 million club option for 2027 with a $250,000 buyout. He is the fourth reliever the Yankees have signed this offseason, joining David Bednar (accepted qualifying offer), Tim Hill, and Jonathan Loáisiga.

    With the bullpen mostly assembled, the Yankees figure to pivot to offense the rest of the offseason. They need a third base upgrade over Ryan McMahon and a right-handed hitting catcher to pair with the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. It seems likely the Yankees will go with Anthony Volpe at second base and Spencer Jones in center field, but those positions can be improved as well.

    The Mets have agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, reports the Newly introduced York Post. It's a one-year deal worth $8 million, according to The Athletic. He will presumably pair with Jared Young in a first base platoon. We did not rank Goldschmidt, 39, among our top 50 free agents. He accepted a reduced role for the Yankees over the last two seasons and was a valuable clubhouse presence.

    At this point in his career, Goldschmidt is no longer an everyday player, but he remains a solid platoon bat. He hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties over the last two years, compared to .235/.271/.337 against righties. Goldschmidt can still play a nifty first base as well. The Mets received the worst first base production in the sport in 2027. Even late-career Goldschmidt should be an upgrade.

    After missing out on Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays are now believed to be prioritizing Freddy Peralta, according to MLB Network. Toronto has a very good one-two punch in Dylan Cease and José Soriano. Behind them are Spencer Arrighetti, Cody Ponce (returning from a torn ACL), Trey Yesavage, and maybe Jake Bloss and Ricky Tiedemann. There's room for another starter, for sure.

    Peralta, Michael King, and Trevor Rogers are the best available free agent starters now that Skubal has signed. Rogers declined the qualifying offer and is attached to draft pick compensation, which perhaps makes King or Peralta more desirable. Any of the three would boost a Blue Jays rotation that has upside but not much in the way of reliability behind Cease and Soriano.

    Industry observers note that the Dodgers are not expected to aggressively pursue pitching help after losing out on Tarik Skubal, reports The Athletic. They're comfortable letting things play out and seeing what shakes loose among second- and third-tier free agents. As much as the Dodgers would have liked to retain Skubal, they're in a spot where they didn't absolutely need him.

    Despite this year's biceps and knee injuries, Shohei Ohtani is expected to pitch next season. He'll join Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Blake Snell, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the rotation. Emmet Sheehan, Gavin Stone, and Justin Wrobleski are next in line, with prospects Jackson Ferris and Christian Zazueta not far away. The Dodgers could use another starter but aren't desperate for one.

    The Mariners, Padres, and Phillies are among the teams interested in Red Sox outfielder Jarred Duran, according to MassLive. The Red Sox tendered Duran a contract at Friday's deadline and will now look to trade him. The Jake Bauers signing pushed Duran, who had a .266 on-base percentage in 2026, out of the regular lineup. A trade is the logical next step.

    Philadelphia and San Diego badly need outfield help and are obvious fits for Duran. Even if the Mariners manage to re-sign Randy Arozarena, they could use another outfielder, though Duran would be a less-than-stellar fit for a lineup that is already heavily left-handed. Regardless, it seems unlikely Duran will be with the Red Sox by the time Opening Day arrives.

    The Blue Jays, Phillies, and Yankees are considered the favorites for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports MLB.com. The Cubs and Mets are believed to have interest as well. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers but is not regarded as a strong defender, and it is likely that he will play first base or a corner outfield spot in MLB.

    Industry observers note that this past season, Sato, 28 in March, hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs and won Japan's Triple Crown. He is similar to Munetaka Murakami in that he has big left-handed power, swing-and-miss concerns, and defensive issues. Murakami is a much more patient hitter, however. Sato is an aggressive swinger and is unlikely to walk much or post a strong on-base percentage.

    Sources indicate that the Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract in the $400 million range before he signed with the Mets, according to The Athletic. Meanwhile, the Dodgers never reached the point of making Skubal an offer, reports ESPN. Los Angeles was known to prefer a short-term, high-dollar contract to a long-term arrangement. Getting Skubal on such a deal always seemed unlikely.

    Industry observers note that as for the Padres, they put forth an offer in the $400 million range but with deferrals that would have lowered the present day value, reports the Fresh York Post. Skubal's contract with the Mets includes $30 million in deferred money, which will lower the present day value some, but not significantly. The exact deferrals in San Diego's offer are unknown.

    The Royals and left-handed reliever Caleb Theilbar are in agreement on a one-year deal, per ESPN. Theilbar, 39, was excellent for the Cubs in 2025, but took a step back in 2026, pitching to a 4.86 ERA (87 ERA+) and 1.30 WHIP with 60 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched. He did strand 18 of the 23 runners he inherited, which is an adequate clip for a middle-relief type.

    The Royals recently acquired late-inning lefty José Ferrer in a trade and Daniel Lynch remains in the bullpen, so Thielbar could well be their third option as a lefty in relief.
