    According to recent reports, welcome to Snyder's Soapbox! Here, I pontificate about matters related to Major League Baseball on a weekly basis. Some of the topics will be pressing matters, some might seem insignificant in the grand scheme of things, and most will be somewhere in between. The good thing about this website is that it's free, and you are allowed to click away. If you stay, you'll get smarter, though. That's a money-back guarantee. Let's get to it.

    According to recent reports, the world of Major League Baseball -- which includes fans and media, too -- has something rather heavy hanging over its head this offseason. Obviously. We know all about that pesky CBA expiration on Dec. 1 and we know that the owners are all but certain to lock the players out that night while they push for a salary cap in the name of parity.

    It has been revealed that people are going to take sides, and I make no apologies for being firmly on the players' side. They are the talent and why we watch the games. No one is buying owners' jerseys and sitting in the ballpark facing the suites.

    Another reason I'm not a huge fan, in general, of the owners is that I don't believe we're ever getting the full truth about how much money they make. The Braves are publicly traded and we can see a good breakdown of how they fared in 2025. The short version is that they are swimming in money. We could look at the two recently sold MLB teams for a hint, too. The Angels were sold for $4 billion; Arte Moreno bought the team for $184 million in 2003. The Padres were also sold recently for $3.9 billion. The San Diego media market size ranks ahead of only Kansas City, Cincinnati, Milwaukee and, eventually, Las Vegas among MLB cities.

    And, again, sometimes you'll have an owner say the quiet part out loud. Enter Orioles owner David Rubenstein:.

    In a recent development, "A lot of my friends were buying teams, and I realized they're making money. They're making more money than I'm making in private equity," Rubenstein noted last month at a forum with other pro sports owners at the Economic Club of Washington, D.C.

    " ... I couldn't figure out why it is that people who are fans are so obsessed with the success of their local team. They're not going to make any more money. They're not going to go to the Super Bowl and get a trophy out of it.".

    People who cape for the owners: this is what you are defending.

    Obviously every owner shouldn't be painted with the same brush. Some of them are legitimately fans. But I'd be willing to wager pretty heavily that a majority of the owners think like Rubenstein here and view the teams simply as vehicles to make as much money as possible.

    Do we even need to bother with the suggestion that we shouldn't care about our favorite teams since they don't make us money and we don't get pieces of metal trophies? Sports fandom can be one of the purest and most wholesome things about our society. It brings families and friends together. It gives us emotions we otherwise couldn't even possibly imagine feeling. And I'll say this, too: I've seen my favorite team win the World Series and the absolute last thing on my mind was, "man, I'd sure like a trophy for my own mantle." The memories can't be matched by anything material at all. I would take nothing of real, tangible substance over those memories.

    It's maddening that an owner can be so out of touch with the product that he purchased.

    Recent findings suggest that do please hone in on the money comment, though. That's a much bigger deal. We've heard owners of some smaller-market teams cry poor for years and even decades, and the response from the MLBPA every single time is a pretty simple one. I reached out to a source and heard it again: "If any team wants us to believe they are losing money, they can simply open their books.".

    According to recent reports, yes. The Braves have to and we can see how much of a money machine they are in the 11th-ranked media market (counting the two-team cities twice).

    It has been revealed that again, there will be exceptions, but the owners generally just view their teams as virtual ATMs, the output of which would be even higher with artificially decreased payroll because of a salary cap. At least one of them doesn't even understand why we care as much as we do.

    I remain firmly and proudly Team MLBPA.

    Thanksgiving Beef: Nick Sirianni vs. fan, Andy Reid vs. the refs, Aaron Rodgers vs. the world

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This Thanksgiving in the NFL was arguably the best in football history, as it marked the first time every matchup featured a game-winning field goal or touchdown in the final five seconds of regulation, according to CBS Sports Research.
    • It has been revealed that there were plenty of heroes from Thursday.
    • There were sideline spats, questionable calls from the officials, upset fan bases, and then, of course, the grenade Aaron Rodgers lobbed at the Pittsburgh Steelers on his way out.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This Thanksgiving in the NFL was arguably the best in football history, as it marked the first time every matchup featured a game-winning field goal or touchdown in the final five seconds of regulation, according to CBS Sports Research.

    It has been revealed that there were plenty of heroes from Thursday. Caleb Williams connected with Rome Odunze in the corner of the end zone with three seconds remaining to beat the Detroit Lions; Jake Elliott of the Philadelphia Eagles capped the largest comeback (21 points) on Thanksgiving in NFL history with a 59-yard field goal to upset the Dallas Cowboys; then Tyler Bass knocked through a 57-yard field goal as time expired to move the Buffalo Bills past the Kansas City Chiefs. It wasn't all sunshine and rainbows on this holiday, however.

    There were sideline spats, questionable calls from the officials, upset fan bases, and then, of course, the grenade Aaron Rodgers lobbed at the Pittsburgh Steelers on his way out. Mike Tomlin finally gave his thoughts on that wild situation Thanksgiving night.

    Below, we will power-rank all the "Thanksgiving Beef" we saw this week.

    Cameras captured Eagles running back Will Shipley having a heated argument with head coach Nick Sirianni during Thursday's matchup in Dallas. It's true that Philly's lead man is known for his emotion, but this looked a bit weird.

    Recent findings suggest that nick Sirianni And Will Shipley Getting Heated On The Sideline.Saquon Barkley Was Part Of This One Too.Not Exactly A Peaceful Thanksgiving In Philly.Something Clearly Has Them All Fired Up. pic.twitter.com/pCzsNMqcnz.

    After the Eagles' incredible 39-38 victory, Shipley told reporters that everything was fine, and cameras just happened to catch a Thanksgiving family argument.

    In a recent development, "Emotions were running high. Like on Thanksgiving, all families are arguing about politics and the drunk uncle," Shipley said with a smile. "I've got so much love for coach Nick and him as the leader of this football team...".

    Will Shipley on his sideline argument with Nick Sirianni pic.twitter.com/AUWxWgJ4An.

    Shipley isn't lying. Apparently he and Sirianni were acting like best friends in the locker room.

    Sources indicate that "They were loving each other up [in the locker room]," left tackle Jordan Mailata said, per ESPN. "I was like, 'Oh, how come I'm not getting hugged like that?'".

    Thursday's edition of Patrick Mahomes vs. Josh Allen was a slugfest that featured just 23 total points scored. The bad weather made every play matter more.

    Sources indicate that with under two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and the game tied at 10 apiece, Mahomes appeared to connect with Rashee Rice over the middle for a first down. However, the NFL headquarters in Newly introduced York chimed in, saying it was actually an incomplete pass.

    In a recent development, WOW... Refs called this a catch on the field but after review overturned the call and ruled this an incomplete catch for the Chiefs... Very little movement on this ball to overturn that pic.twitter.com/5yZ6sMQqTr.

    Sources indicate that chiefs head coach Andy Reid disagreed with the call and blamed "Newly introduced York" for the reversal. The refs on the field had the correct ruling, but the league's headquarters did not, he remarked.

    "Not one that I agreed with, but they said that this came from New York," Reid said. "It's not from these guys; our guys called it a completion — the guys who were working the game. I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit, then the ball hit. But he had control. Normally, in those kinds of situations, it's got to be clear and obvious. And to me, that was not clear and obvious.".

    According to recent reports, this was a pivotal moment that forced the Chiefs to punt. Kansas City ended the game with two straight three-and-outs.

    The 5-7 Cowboys fell to third place in the NFC East with their Thanksgiving loss to the Eagles. It's been an embarrassing season for Dallas, as the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to average 30 points per game and have a losing record through 12 games. NFL teams are a combined 75-2-1 this year when up by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter. The Cowboys have registered both of those losses.

    Think about all the ways the Cowboys hurt their fan base:.

    How much worse can it get? After the loss to the Eagles, who's to say the Cowboys aren't the worst team in this stinky division?

    Industry observers note that following the Eagles' game-winning field goal, Sirianni went to celebrate with some Philly fans near the field. However, it looked like he wanted to confront one of the fans, and he was yanked back by chief security officer Dom DiSandro and another staffer.

    What is Nick Sirianni doing??? pic.twitter.com/vcJ8cIUmDd.

    Sirianni attempted to play this moment down, telling reporters that his staffers just wanted to get him back on the field to shake hands with Schottenheimer. I doubt that.

    It has been revealed that there was a ... let's call him a very vocal fan who would like Sirianni fired, in that section. Even after the Eagles won the game, he was flipping his head coach the bird.

    Nick Sirianni was fired up after one of the best comebacks in Eagles history against their biggest rival in Dallas pic.twitter.com/PgDTrsRio4.

    There are other vulgar videos you can find online of this dude, but Sirianni definitely wanted a piece of him. Wouldn't that have been something? A head coach fighting one of his own fans moments after a massive game-winning field goal?

    Rodgers was benched by the Steelers this week, so he went scorched-earth on the franchise. He didn't exactly throw a tantrum, but instead went a different, more calculated route — painting head coach Mike McCarthy as an old, unhealthy man totally incapable of leading an NFL franchise during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    Rodgers accused his now-former coach of a lot, from falling asleep in meetings and failing to prepare for games to failing to connect with his players. The breaking point, according to Rodgers, was when McCarthy broke down the team saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" at halftime of last Sunday's loss to the Eagles. McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018.

    Rodgers' public undressing of his former boss will go down as one of the craziest "beefs" in NFL history — and it's generated plenty of response. There are former teammates of Rodgers who did not approve of what he did. T.J. Lang called it "despicable," while Greg Jennings called it "distasteful." Even Tom Brady noted Rodgers violated "the sanctity of the NFL locker room.".

    Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin spoke out on Thursday night, calling the situation a "dumpster fire.".

    "I'm upset about it; it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin mentioned. "And I don't say that in a judgemental way; I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset.".

    This "Turkey Day Beef" could hurt Rodgers' legacy, and it's a story that's not over just yet.

    • Recent findings suggest that victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words.
    • According to recent reports, so here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday.
    • Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words. Stephen Curry is the only player I can remember thinking of the same way in the post-Michael Jordan era. Nobody else. With Steph and Wemby, you can't fully describe what you've seen. You try, but in the end you just have to see them to understand. It's totally different than anything you've ever witnessed on a basketball court.

    According to recent reports, so here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday. It feels like we're qualifying one of his "first in history" stat lines about once a week, and indeed, Wembanyama is the first player since blocks and steals became an official stat in 1973 to record those single-game numbers.

    Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.

    VICTOR WEMBANYAMA BECOMES THE FIRST PLAYER SINCE 1973-74 TO RECORD 50+ PTS, 15+ REB, 4+ STL AND 5+ BLK IN A GAME!🤯 50 PTS🤯 18 REB🤯 5 BLK🤯 4 STL🤯 5 3PM🤯 32 MINSPURS WIN THEIR 14TH IN 15 GAMES. pic.twitter.com/lPKk3jYNjL.

    Before the halftime buzzer had even sounded, Wembanyama had already tallied 32 points, 13 rebounds, three steals and three blocks. That would be a career game for a lot of NBA players. He had played 18 minutes. You can only laugh at this point.

    What was even funnier, however, was Wembanyama's comment after the game, when he took a clear stab at, well, whoever he considers his "peers" to be by calling them out for, shall we say, unethical statistical pursuits.

    According to recent reports, "It is very special," Wembanyama said of reaching the 50-point mark for the second time this season and third time in his career. "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not good at stat-padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have.".

    Victor Wembanyama after scoring 50 points: “Unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at statpadding.” pic.twitter.com/OAogFCa2oi.

    So here's what's interesting about this little dig: Wembanyama was definitely guilty of stat-padding his way to 50 in this game. With just more than eight minutes remaining and the Spurs up by 24, Wembanyama could've stayed on the bench after the timeout. The Spurs have made a concerted effort to limit his minutes whenever possible this year. Even in the golden age of comebacks, this game was over.

    But Wemby stayed in and proceeded to take five straight shots on the next five possessions. He was hunting the 50. No question about it. He even admitted as much.

    In a recent development, "The greats of the game, they don't care [about stat-padding]," Wemby stated, via The Athletic. "I don't think Wilt [Chamberlain] thought about that when he had 98 points. ... That stepback 3, going right, that I took, it doesn't correlate with this. It didn't fit to the definition [of ethical basketball], for example. So I did try [to stat-pad] at the end.".

    According to recent reports, good on Wemby for acknowledging his own hypocrisy, but it raises the question: if you just did the very thing you are railing against, why take the jab in the first place? Every player who has been within range of 50 points has gone for it as long as it's not a competitive game in which quality shots still matter. It's not that major a deal.

    But Wemby has done this before. In December of 2025, after the Spurs had just defeated the Thunder, he said, "I'm just glad to be part of something that's growing to be so beautiful — pure and ethical basketball.".

    According to recent reports, this was a definite jab at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-baiting. Wemby, meanwhile, has turned into one of the more theatrical floppers in the league. In almost every way, Wembanyama is different than any other basketball player in the world. But when it comes to this ethical, non-stat-padding basketball soapbox he has climbed upon on numerous occasions, the truth is he's just like everyone else. So enough with the jabs.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked the undersized Taira as the No.
    • "Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After missing out on bigger name free agent starting pitchers like Tarik Skubal, Trevor Rogers, and Freddy Peralta, the Toronto Blue Jays have fortified their rotation by signing free agent right-hander Kaima Taira out of Japan. The deal is for $80 million over five years with an opt-out after the third year, the Latest York Post reports.

    Earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked the undersized Taira as the No. 19 free agent of the current 2026-27 class. Here's part of that write-up:.

    "Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu announced on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.".

    Sources indicate that for his NPB career, Taira has a 1.85 ERA with 676 strikeouts in 633 ⅔ innings in a mix of rotation and bullpen duty. While, as noted above, Taira may not profile as a starter in MLB, the Jays will likely give him every opportunity to stick in their rotation, given their need there behind ace Dylan Cease. In addition to the $80 million commitment to Taira, the Jays will owe his former team, the Seibu Lions, a posting fee per the MLB-NPB agreement.

    Toronto won the pennant in 2025 but backslid in 2026 to 83 losses and a last-place finish in the American League East. The offense was their leading liability last season, but the rotation also needed attention. That explains why they were very much in the bidding for Skubal and other premium starting pitchers on the market. It furthermore explains why they're willing to take a chance on Taira.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

    Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

    His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

    Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

    Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

    United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

    United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

    Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

    But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

    At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his newly introduced role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

    In a recent development, “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

    “I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

    “But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

    “Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

    It has been revealed that welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

    At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri noted Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

    Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

    Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, upcoming signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.
    • Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.
    • The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

    The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

    Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

    Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

    Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

    'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

    Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary.

    Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

    Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights.

    Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

    Sources indicate that 'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen said in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

    'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

    According to recent reports, 'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

    The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

    Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

    'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he said. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'.

    'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

    'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'.

    Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

    But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties presently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

    'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

    Industry observers note that 'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

    When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

    Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

    The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication.

    Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend.

    Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

    It has been revealed that 'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health concerns Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

    Industry observers note that 'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'.

    Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

    'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

    Sources indicate that 'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

    'Money has become more notable than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

    Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how notable 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

    'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg said, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

    Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

    He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

    After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

    Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical issues.

    Recent findings suggest that 'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

    Recent findings suggest that 'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

    According to recent reports, 'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'.

    2027 NFL Draft: Remaining games that will determine the draft order, including No. 1 overall

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With seven weeks remaining in the regular season, the first-round draft order is far from settled.
    • Full draft order and needs, free agents for each team.
    • The NFC South is heavily represented because three of the four teams have just three wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With seven weeks remaining in the regular season, the first-round draft order is far from settled. Several head-to-head matchups between teams near the bottom of the standings could have a significant impact on where each franchise ultimately selects. Which remaining games could have the biggest implications for the 2027 NFL Draft?

    Full draft order and needs, free agents for each team.

    The NFC South is heavily represented because three of the four teams have just three wins. With four games remaining among those three teams, the draft order will take care of itself in time.

    When the two teams met earlier this season, Atlanta won by three touchdowns. It would be interesting to learn whether the Falcons would explore drafting another quarterback in the first round three years after taking Michael Penix Jr.

    Tampa Bay has looked like a dominant team at times and lethally flawed at others. The health of Baker Mayfield has played a substantial role in the team's misfortunes, but the quarterback's stubborn tendencies also lead one to wonder if he may be too injured to help the team right now.

    The Buccaneers dominated a prior meeting, 16-0.

    If Upcoming Orleans were to lose out, difficult conversations may be had regarding head coach Kellen Moore. Kevin Stefanski has a longer leash in Atlanta. The two teams meet in Week 18 as well.

    Industry observers note that tampa Bay has not picked Top-10 overall since taking linebacker Devin White No. 5 overall in 2019. Four of Atlanta's last six first-round picks have been within the Top-10 overall.

    Los Angeles broke an eight-game losing streak two weeks ago against the Ravens. Will they find another victory by season's end? Among teams with just one win this season, Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers may be feeling the most pressure. Harbaugh is in his third season with the franchise, while the other two head coaches are in their first.

    On the opposite sideline, Tampa Bay head coach Todd Bowles may also be coaching for his job over the remainder of the season.

    Beyond the teams with a league-low one victory, the exercise meant taking a stance against certain teams. Arizona has fired its defensive coordinator and is now testing the depths of its quarterback position. Jacoby Brissett was traded, and Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck suffered injuries. The Cardinals are not a threat down the stretch, so it is less likely they will string together some wins and fall outside the Top-10.

    Philadelphia stole a win against in-state rival Pittsburgh, but quarterback Joe Milton is unlikely to stack multiple wins in the final weeks of the season. The Eagles also seemingly acknowledged the season was lost by trading defensive tackle Jordan Davis.

    Arizona was feisty early in the season, but injuries to the offensive line and running back set them on a different course. The team lacks difference-makers in the passing game apart from tight end Trey McBride.

    Recent findings suggest that new Orleans was hot at the end of the 2025 season and carried that momentum into the offseason. However, injuries to key performers, such as running back Travis Etienne and wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, along with roster limitations, promptly set in.

    Jets head coach Aaron Glenn came into the season knowing his job was on the line if the team didn't meet expectations. As a result, the team brought in veteran quarterback Geno Smith and several other veterans to raise the team's floor. Reality quickly set in for the franchise despite early-season hope. The Jets will once again have three first-round picks, but will Glenn be around to advise them?

    One would assume Cardinals head coach Matt LaFleur is not in danger of losing his job, so an opportunity to build this team in his image lies ahead. The first order of business will be identifying and securing the correct quarterback.

    These two teams are presently in position to draft Top-5 overall. If Miami wins, the same will be true next week. Although unlikely to get the No. 1 overall selection, New York has a vested interest in remaining near the top of the draft order so it isn't outside striking distance for a potential trade up for its quarterback of choice. In theory, such a move would cost less if the team only moved up a few spots.

    Indianapolis is obviously not in possession of its own first-round pick, but the Jets will make that selection. As you're reading this, the Colts have moved on from Daniel Jones, so there isn't much upside left to the team's season. Indianapolis will almost certainly send a Top-10 overall pick back to Newly introduced York as part of the Sauce Gardner trade.

    Sources indicate that tennessee is currently in pole position and may be another team disinterested in taking a No. 1 overall quarterback if Cam Ward continues to show progress.

    Three teams have one loss, and two of them will play in the final weeks of the regular season. Beyond affecting the draft order, this could also determine whether the No. 1 overall selection is available for trade. Los Angeles is presumably tied to quarterback Justin Herbert, whereas Miami is expected to be in the market for a quarterback. If the Chargers had the No. 1 overall pick, they could prioritize trading it to a franchise looking for a quarterback or to acquire Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

    #166279. Ranking NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Knicks hit their stride, while Celtics take step back

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1692 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Ranking NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Knicks hit their stride, while Celtics take step back

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season.
    • The Western Conference is similarly crunched.
    • Recent findings suggest that you're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans, aren't you?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season. Take a look at the standings right now. The No. 2 through the No. 6 seeds in the Eastern Conference standings all have exactly six losses, and while the Philadelphia 76ers hold a three-game lead for the No. 1 seed, they've done so behind a preposterous 12-0 clutch record. When they regress to the mean, we seem destined for an Eastern Conference packed like sardines.

    The Western Conference is similarly crunched. The San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the standings with identical 14-3 records... but seeds 3-9 are all separated by no more than two games. Even the Sacramento Kings got a win this week! The NBA has spent years tinkering in order to create parity, and right now, at least it's getting it. With that unofficial week of parity in the books, let's crown some winners and losers from the last seven days.

    Recent findings suggest that you're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans, aren't you? That'd be the easy starting point. We could just as easily kick things off with Luka Dončić's shooting dip, as he has quietly shot roughly 41-31-82 in his past five games, bringing his ridiculous offensive numbers down to slightly more mortal levels and making Wembanyama, for now, the slight MVP betting favorite. Totally reasonable. They're both contributors to his excellent week.

    Recent findings suggest that neither stands up to what Wembanyama did against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. He shunked. That's a word that didn't exist when we woke up on Thursday. It is now, hilariously, a signature moment of Wembanyama's young career. He has apparently dunked so often, so violently that he suffered a hand injury that compelled him to try, and succeed, to shoot a jump shot at the rim.

    Did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    Sources indicate that the MVP race is for the season. The ridiculous numbers are for the history books. The shunk wins the week. Any time you suffer and overcome a dunking-related injury by inventing a upcoming form of scoring, you win the week.

    In a recent development, the champs have won five in a row and are 11-3 overall since their 0-3 start, but this isn't as simple as the Knicks suddenly looking like the Knicks again. Many of the early season problems are still persisting. Mikal Bridges hit the game-winner on Friday and still shot 3-of-12 on Sunday. Josh Hart missed all four of his 3-pointers on Sunday and is below 26% shooting from deep so far this season. The starters, as a group, are still getting outscored by almost 13 points per 100 possessions after struggling mightily in the past two regular seasons.

    Sources indicate that yet they just keep winning. There are obvious basketball reasons for that. Karl-Anthony Towns is getting every rebound, making every shot, and has readopted the playmaking hub role he thrived in throughout the postseason, particularly when it comes to assisting Jalen Brunson. The bench is thriving. Landry Shamet is shooting better than 45% on 3s and Deuce McBride isn't far behind. Tyler Kolek has a 61-to-9 assist-to-turnover ratio.

    Industry observers note that but there's something deeper here, a resilience and versatility that developed over last season's championship run that is sustaining thus far this season. OG Anunoby has missed the past two games. Towns missed the Blazers game. Bridges and Hart play most of some games and only parts of others because of their early season struggles. Yet Mike Brown just keeps pulling the right levers, and the Knicks just keep figuring it out. Championships can bring about this certainty. The Knicks aren't quite themselves yet, but they have an internalized confidence that came from dominating the playoff crucible a year ago that's paying off handsomely right now.

    Recent findings suggest that it's hard to tell what we've seen from the Heat thus far this season that really deserves scrutiny. They started 0-4 in part because opponents weren't missing any 3s. They've gone 8-2 since, but they haven't beaten a single notable, fully healthy opponent during their active seven-game winning streak. No Evan Mobley against the Cleveland Cavaliers. No Jalen Duren against the Detroit Pistons. No Amen Thompson against the Houston Rockets. No... basically anyone against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, though in fairness, Giannis Antetokounmpo missed that game himself. Miami is something of a Rorschach test so far. You're going to see what you're predisposed to seeing.

    But if we're going to panic during the shooting luck-induced losing streak, we're going to have to acknowledge the positives during the winning streak. The maligned Heat offense ranks in the top five over their past 10 games largely because Klay Thompson is shooting like Klay Thompson again and Giannis Antetokounmpo never stopped dunking like Giannis Antetokounmpo. Their core lineups featuring Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are deterring rim attempts and giving up basically no corner 3s. Andrew Wiggins looks more like Andrew Wiggins since moving to the bench. As tempted as I was to give the third slot to the player development coaches for the Memphis Grizzlies after Cam Spencer's breakout 26-point game against Cleveland, the seven-game Miami winning streak gets the nod.

    The Celtics were too clever by a half with their lineup decisions this weekend. They sat Jayson Tatum and Derrick White against the hapless Kings and then sat Paul George in the second half of that back-to-back against the Stephen Curry-less Golden State Warriors. They lost both very winnable games by a single point when they probably could have ensured a split and maybe even a sweep by aligning the rest. Throw in a 17-point blown lead to the Denver Nuggets and allowing a 40-point fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic and the previously 11-2 Celtics lost all four of their games this week. They're back with the Eastern Conference pack.

    It's too early to draw any real conclusions, just as it was too early to crown them Eastern Conference favorites when they were throttling the Sixers two weeks ago, but this week was a reminder of some of the cracks here. Their best player is coming off of a torn Achilles, and their second- and third-best players are in their 30s and have to be managed carefully throughout the season. You can get away with never getting to the basket as a team when you're an elite 3-point shooting outfit. The Celtics haven't been this season, and we're now in Year 2 of Derrick White's 3-point drought (and, for that matter, arguably Year 3 of Jayson Tatum's). Mitchell Robinson will put together a few good stretches and then regress back into the mess he's been for most of the season. Boston has been nearly 22 points stronger per 100 possessions with him off the floor this season.

    The Celtics, given their playing style and roster makeup, are vulnerable to the ebbs and flows of an 82-game season. When everyone's available and they're making their shots, they're going to look unbeatable. This week is what happens when they're not, and considering how frequently that's been the case for them in the playoffs, it's something the Celtics are going to have to learn to play through if they hope to make it through this crowded East.

    Slowly but surely, the NBA's cellar dwellers are starting to come around. The Utah Jazz won twice this week. The Chicago Bulls have won three times since Caleb Wilson went down, and they pushed the Denver Nuggets to overtime on Sunday. The Kings got win No. 2 on Saturday, but also pushed the Los Angeles Lakers to the brink on Friday. There is still a whole lot of misery at the bottom of the standings, but all of these teams can find small pockets of optimism.

    Industry observers note that not the Bucks, who are now the NBA's last one-win team and owners of a 13-game losing streak. One of those losses came against Miami this week as their former franchise player, Antetokounmpo, throttled them for three quarters before they made the final score look respectable in the fourth quarter. They have the NBA's worst defense comfortably. Beyond a three-game stretch in which second-year guard Kasparas Jakučionis averaged 21 points per game, it's simply been a miserable season in Milwaukee, and it's one that could get worse any day now as the NBA investigates potential salary cap circumvention involving Gary Trent Jr. We all knew the Bucks would struggle with post-Giannis life, but this is worse than anyone could have imagined.

    Tyrese Haliburton has played four games this season at a roughly All-Star level. The Indiana Pacers are now 3-10 in all other contests, and ESPN reported Friday that Haliburton is set to miss at least another few weeks with a left hamstring strain. This is after a 19-win season played entirely without Haliburton a year ago. At this point, obvious as it sounds, it's simply become clear that the Pacers can't win consistently without their best player. That was obvious in a playoff context, but the regular-season implications here are starting to add up.

    Industry observers note that indiana is already six games out of a top-six Eastern Conference seed. Even when Haliburton gets back, he's probably not going to be perfectly healthy for the entire rest of the season just given his own history of durability concerns. The East's bottom four teams are thankfully so dreadful that there's probably a floor of No. 11 here, but Indiana will eventually have to pass someone -- presumably the Washington Wizards, perhaps someone else who gets bitten by the injury bug -- just to make it back into the Play-In Tournament picture. Even if they're there, their road to and through the playoffs becomes enormously precarious. It doesn't matter how dangerous you are in a playoff setting if you can't actually survive the regular season and make it there. It's too early to say that's where Indiana is headed, but the danger is very real.

    • It has been revealed that earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked Peralta as the No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that veteran right-handed starter Freddy Peralta has signed with the Baltimore Orioles on a five-year deal, the team declared on Tuesday. The contract is worth $125 million with no deferrals or options, The Athletic reports.

    Peralta, who will be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is coming off a campaign in which he didn't pitch up to his usual standards during a disastrous stint with the New York Mets. However, he did more like his old self following a deadline trade to the Tampa Bay Rays. On the Rays' watch, Peralta made a series of adjustments that helped him find better results on the mound, including being named the ALCS MVP.

    It has been revealed that earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked Peralta as the No. 7 free agent of the 2026-27 class. Here's part of our write-up:.

    Recent findings suggest that "It has been a roller coaster year for Peralta, who flopped with the Mets, rebounded with the Rays, then faced the Brewers (his former team) in the World Series and lost. The post-deadline stint with Tampa salvaged Peralta's free agent year. They made several adjustments, most notably raising his arm angle and getting him to pitch exclusively from the stretch, and the result was a livelier fastball and also better command. He's still five-and-fly Freddy. Even the best version of Peralta won't pitch deep into games and can be a tough watch because he nibbles and throws so many pitches per inning. They tend to be good innings, though, and the guy never misses a start. Worst case, Peralta is a mid-rotation starter you can count on to take the ball every fifth day. The best case is someone who can front a contender's rotation. Fastball Freddy was always going to be a great bounceback candidate this offseason. The Rays just beat everyone to it at the trade deadline.".

    Industry observers note that peralta isn't far removed from a 2023-25 stretch for the Milwaukee Brewers that saw him top 30 starts and 200 strikeouts in three straight seasons. In 2025, he earned his second All-Star selection and finished fifth in the National League Cy Young vote.

    Industry observers note that "Freddy has proven to be a winning player who understands what it takes to compete and succeed on the biggest stage," stated Orioles president of baseball operations Mike Elias said in a statement. "His professionalism, preparation, and commitment to winning will set a strong example for our organization and we believe he will have a significant impact on our team both on and off the field.".

    Sources indicate that after losing Trevor Rogers to free agency (he agreed to a five-year contract with the Chicago Cubs earlier on Tuesday), the Orioles were searching for a new frontline starter to join a rotation that includes Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and some combination of Brandon Young, Cade Povich and Trey Gibson. Elias has been hesitant to pay up for pitchers recently, but either his strategy has changed or he decided Peralta was worth the cost.

    The Orioles' disappointing fourth-place AL East finish in 2026 has raised questions about the state of Baltimore's rebuild, particularly amid stalled growth from its promising young position players, including Jackson Holliday, Gunnar Henderson and Colton Cowser. Would-be franchise backstop Adley Rutschman was traded to the Boston Red Sox at the trade deadline.

    Because Peralta was traded during the 2026 season and was thus ineligible for the qualifying offer, the Orioles will not be penalized a draft pick for signing him.

    Latest Update: Steelers vs. Broncos prediction: Why Mason Rudolph can lead upset after Aaron Rodgers drama

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1343 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This Black Friday showdown was already a must-watch before this week's stunning events in Pittsburgh, which led to Aaron Rodgers' release.
    • Sources indicate that despite this week's turmoil and a two-game losing streak, Pittsburgh (6-4) is still right now on the inside track in the AFC playoff picture.
    • Denver started the season slowly but has since won six straight games on the strength of an offense that has scored at least 23 points in five of those wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This Black Friday showdown was already a must-watch before this week's stunning events in Pittsburgh, which led to Aaron Rodgers' release. That news has added even more interest around a game that will have major playoff implications.

    Sources indicate that despite this week's turmoil and a two-game losing streak, Pittsburgh (6-4) is still right now on the inside track in the AFC playoff picture. But the Steelers' season is entering a pivotal stretch with upcoming games against Denver, Houston and Jacksonville.

    Denver started the season slowly but has since won six straight games on the strength of an offense that has scored at least 23 points in five of those wins. However, now they'll have a latest quarterback and plenty of baggage heading into Friday.

    Here's how to follow the action in real time, along with a preview and prediction on how Mason Rudolph can pull off an upset.

    Industry observers note that rodgers took every first-team rep during Tuesday's practice. By 11:10 that night, the Steelers had benched him and made him inactive for Friday's game. Fast forward less than 24 hours later, and the Steelers had released Rodgers after he scorched Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    It has been revealed that what caused the breakup? Rodgers did not feel that McCarthy should be the team's play-caller and gave him an ultimatum: Let either him or QB coach Tom Arth call the plays, or release him. McCarthy called his bluff.

    The Steelers' offense will now be led by Mason Rudolph, a nine-year veteran with 20 career starts, including one postseason start.

    Rudolph delivered when he was put in a similar spot back in 2023. He led the Steelers to three late-season wins that allowed Pittsburgh to clinch a spot in the playoffs.

    Sources indicate that now 31, Rudolph doesn't exactly excel at anything, but he is a solid pro who can move an offense. He's largely accurate and has had success in the past on deep passes. Rudolph also has the respect of his teammates and coaches.

    "I feel really good about Mason," McCarthy said on Wednesday. "I don't (want to) say pleasantly surprised, because that wouldn't be fair to him and what he's accomplished before we began working together. I think Tom Arth has done a great job with Mason and the young guys. He's done everything we ask as far as how to play, and has done a great job in the number two slot with the reps, and getting ready to play.".

    According to recent reports, rudolph will have some extra help against Denver. Michael Pittman, a former 1,100-yard receiver for the Colts, will play for the first time since Week 4. Roman Wilson made his return to the lineup last week and caught three passes for 43 yards. Fellow wideout Max Hurleman caught six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown on Sunday in his regular season debut.

    It has been revealed that those players will help, but the Steelers' offense will need more production from wideouts DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle if they are going to upset Denver. It's very possible that the Steelers' newfound depth at receiver should help open things up for Metcalf, Bernard and the Steelers' running back duo.

    Rudolph and Co. will face a Broncos defense that is good but not great this season. The unit, which was third in the NFL in fewest points allowed in both 2024 and 2025, is 11th in points allowed this season. They're 24th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, 28th in average yards-per-carry allowed, 20th in third-down efficiency and 10th in red zone efficiency. Essentially, the Broncos have been a bend-but-not-break unit in 2026.

    Pressure and opportunistic plays by the secondary have been Denver's calling card on defense. The Broncos have 31 sacks, with three players tied for the team lead at 5.0. Defensive back Ja'Quan McMillian has filled the stat sheet this season with 3.0 sacks, 39 tackles, two interceptions and eight pass breakups. He and safety Talanoa Hufanga have each returned interceptions for touchdowns.

    Nix has faced Pittsburgh just once before, and it was his second career start back in Week 2 of the 2024 season. Nix and Co. were kept off the scoreboard for three quarters before getting two field goals in the fourth quarter. It wasn't enough as Pittsburgh left Denver with a 13-6 win.

    Sources indicate that nix has mostly won since that game, but his play has regressed since his rookie season. This year, Nix is completing just 59.9% of his passes with 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has yet to throw for over 300 yards in a game and has been held three times under 200 passing yards.

    It has been revealed that it's fair to wonder if Nix is still working his way back from January's severe ankle injury, as it sometimes takes an athlete a full year to get back to where they were pre-injury. Whatever the reason is, it hasn't prevented Nix from winning the majority of his starts.

    One of Denver's greatest strengths on offense is that it seldom turns the ball over. The Broncos have had just one game with multiple turnovers (Week 1) and have turned it over just two times in their last five games. The Broncos' offensive line also does a good job keeping Nix clean, as he has been sacked just 12 times.

    It has been revealed that the Broncos' offense has also been extremely good in the red zone, which has somewhat made up for their struggles on third down (they are 31st in the NFL in third-down efficiency). One of the reasons for Denver's success in the red zone has been their depth at receiver and the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who has run for a team-high six scores. Coleman will continue to be Denver's featured back on Friday as J.K. Dobbins has been suspended for conduct detrimental to the team.

    Pittsburgh's game strategy on defense will be to exploit Denver's porous third-down offense. Patrick Graham's unit will look to make the Broncos' offense one-dimensional by shutting down Coleman and the running game and putting the Broncos into obvious passing situations on third down.

    The substantial question is whether the Steelers will play more man coverage after Joe Burrow and Joe Milton III have had success against their largely zone-based scheme over the last two weeks. It's safe to assume that if the Steelers continue to play heavy zone coverage, Sean Payton will give Nix a bevy of short, safe passes to negate Pittsburgh's pass rush.

    Recent findings suggest that as noted above, the Broncos have depth at receiver, but they don't have any elite wideouts, either. Because of that, the Steelers should play more man without the fear of getting beaten too many times over the top. Pittsburgh's secondary was outmatched two weeks ago in Cincinnati. That shouldn't be the case against Denver.

    On paper, this is a win for the Broncos. They have the better team on both sides of the ball and haven't lost a game since Week 5. Conversely, the Steelers have lost two straight and are coming off a tumultuous week.

    According to recent reports, football games aren't played on paper, though. Upsets happen all the time in the NFL (like the Eagles' upset win in Dallas on Thanksgiving), so no one should be terribly surprised if the Steelers find a way to upset the Broncos at home, where they have yet to lose this season.

    Rudolph isn't a typical backup. He has nine years of experience under his belt, including a playoff start. He has a deep understanding of the Steelers' offense and his offensive teammates. Rudolph will also have his full complement of playmakers, which is something Rodgers never really had this season.

    More than that, Rudolph has risen to the occasion in similar situations in the past, and I expect him to do so once more against the Broncos.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • Free agent catcher Tyler Stephenson has agreed to a three-year contract to return to the Reds, reports ESPN.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Just recently, for instance, the Upcoming York Mets landed the biggest fish in the pond by signing ace Tarik Skubal to a record contract. Not long after, the Chicago Cubs fortified their rotation with Trevor Rogers and their outfield with Teruaki Sato, and Freddy Peralta is headed to the Baltimore Orioles. More's surely to come before lockout day arrives.

    Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Tuesday's supply just below.

    Free agent catcher Tyler Stephenson has agreed to a three-year contract to return to the Reds, reports ESPN. The deal is worth $30 million and includes an opt-out after the second year. Cincinnati selected Stephenson, 30, with the No. 11 pick in the 2015 draft, and he's played his entire career with the Reds. We ranked him as the 46th-best free agent available.

    The Reds will again pair Stephenson with glove-first backup Jose Trevino behind the plate. Cincinnati now figures to turn their attention to the pitching staff, both the rotation and bullpen. Hunter Greene's UCL surgery means Andrew Abbott and Chase Burns are the only locks for the rotation, though Nick Lodolo will have a spot as long as he's healthy.

    Recent findings suggest that the Yankees are among the many teams with interest in top free agent reliever Adrian Morejon, reports the New York Post. Some teams view him as a potential starter, though there were reports earlier this month that he prefers to stay in the bullpen. The Phillies, meanwhile, are not considered a serious candidate to sign Morejon, according to The Athletic. We ranked him as the second-best free agent available this offseason, in part due to his potential to start.

    Adding to the bullpen has been the Yankees' primary focus so far this offseason. Closer David Bednar accepted the qualifying offer, they re-signed lefty matchup guy Tim Hill, and signed Jonathan Loáisiga and Tim Hill as free agents. At some point they will need to add to their lineup, particularly at third base, but there's always room for a reliever like Morejon in the bullpen.

    The Philadelphia Phillies are open to moving Trea Turner off of shortstop given that he's now a pronounced defensive liability. Speaking of openness, veteran shortstop Corey Seager of the Texas Rangers is willing to waive his no-trade clause to join the Phillies and upgrade the position for them, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.

    It has been revealed that now 32, Seager will always have health and durability concerns, but he remains a plus defensive shortstop who produces well at the plate by positional standards. Signed to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season (just before the last lockout, in fact), Seager is owed another $155 million through the 2031 season. The Rangers are reportedly looking to shake things up. The Phillies, meantime, are trying to keep their contention window open. It's a fit both ways, at least in theory. Such a move would likely mean a move to the outfield for Turner, who himself has very little trade value thanks to his ongoing decline and substantial contract.

    Even in a down 2026 year, Jazz Chisholm Jr. put up 19 homers and stole 41 bases while manning an up-the-middle position. Still just 28 years of age, he figures to have a healthy market this offseason. Speaking of which, the Washington Nationals are one of multiple teams presently in contact with Chisholm, FanSided reports.

    Sources indicate that earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Chisholm as the No. 6 free agent in the current class. Here's part of that write-up:.

    Industry observers note that "In what was his worst season as a hitter since his rookie year in 2021, Chisholm was still a league-average bat in 2026, and his top-shelf defense and baserunning still landed him at 3.5 WAR. Chisholm is a style-over-substance player who is not for everyone, but his second base defense and near-MLB-best baserunning skills give him a very high floor. He's a reasonable bet for 20-ish home runs with the potential to go 30-30, and Chisholm has improved his plate discipline enough to run walk rates north of 10% the last two years. The downside is his propensity to swing and miss. Chisholm has posted below-average in-zone contact rates throughout his career and contact rates that low always come with risk. That risk is mitigated somewhat by the secondary skills (defense, etc.) and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29. You probably don't want him as your best or second-best player, but he's also an overqualified No. 6-7 hitter who brings so much else to the table.".

    Sources indicate that the Cleveland Guardians have agreed to a free-agent contract with left-hander Kris Bubic, Sportsnet reports. The contract is for $17.5 million over one year, according to ESPN. Bubic, 29, made nine starts for the Kansas City Royals last season, and after the trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers, he was used out of the bullpen. Bubic has an outlier fastball thanks to its rise and his unusual release point, and he's an interesting "ceiling" candidate in the rotation. However, his substantial history of injuries may mean he's best used out of the bullpen.

    Sources indicate that the Detroit Tigers have added infield depth by agreeing to terms with Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million free agent contract, ESPN reports. Kim, 31, is coming off a rough partial season with the Atlanta Braves, but he has a more palatable OPS+ of 91 for his career. He's been a primary shortstop in recent years and also has significant time spent at second base and third base.

    In a recent development, even after achieving a reunion with veteran starting pitcher Sonny Gray, the Minnesota Twins are still looking to fortify their roster for a return to contention in 2027. The club still hopes to make one more significant addition this offseason and add another player who may not grab as many headlines, the Athletic reports. Atop the wishlist are a first baseman or a second baseman and another lefty reliever.

    Even after the splash addition of Skubal, the Mets may not be done adding starting pitchers in the service of a rebound season in 2027. On that front, the Mets may be interested in adding a starting pitcher on a short-term deal for next season, the Athletic reports. That would likely limit them to the back half of the market, especially with so many bigger names reaching agreements.
