    von Next Generation am 26.05.2025 in den Kategorien Uncategorized,Video Analysis mit 4 Kommentaren.

    Daniel Kahneman was one of the leading psychologists of our time. In his book Thinking, Fast and Slow, he presented extensive insights from his many years of research. This article explores how Kahneman’s findings, along with other insights from behavioral science, can be applied to (strategic and tactical) football analysis.

    Kahneman became well known in the field of behavioral economics. Together with his colleague Amos Tversky, he succeeded in combining insights from psychology with those of economics. In 2002, he became the first psychologist to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.

    According to recent reports, his research challenges the fundamental assumption that humans make rational decisions and that cognitive distortions are primarily driven by emotions. Instead, he argued that systematic thinking errors significantly influence our judgment and decision-making. These systematic errors, known as “biases,” occur in predictable ways under certain conditions.

    Kahneman’s work has been applied in fields such as medical diagnosis, the legal system, intelligence analysis, philosophy, statistics, and military strategy. It is therefore a logical step to apply his research to sports analysis, where strategic decisions also play a crucial role.

    “I suppose that every author has in mind a situation in which readers of their work might benefit from reading it. I imagine the coffee machine at the office, where colleagues exchange opinions and gossip. My hope is to enrich the vocabulary people use when they talk about the judgments and decisions of others (…).” – Daniel Kahneman; Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    Sources indicate that A mere list of cognitive biases is not sufficient to recognize and avoid distortions in one’s own or others’ decisions. Only through a deeper understanding of their origins and mechanisms can the vocabulary around judgment and decision-making be enriched in Kahneman’s sense. Therefore, this article sheds light on the underlying processes and mechanisms of judgment and decision errors.

    We begin by examining the scientifically established dual-process model. Following that, the mechanisms of WYSIATI, substitution, and priming will be explored in the context of football. In addition, the most relevant heuristics and cognitive biases will be applied to football analysis. Finally, we will address individual factors within analysis that contribute to the emergence of bias.

    Industry observers note that this article is only the first part of a series, which will span at least three essays. The series will examine flawed judgments in football analysis and their causes within a scientific framework informed by behavioral research.

    One point should be made clear from the outset: bias (and noise) are present wherever decisions are made, and thus affect even expert judgments within their domain.

    Industry observers note that this article is based on a German translation of Daniel Kahneman’s work. Accordingly, the quotes cited here may not exactly match the original English wording.

    To explain human thinking, Kahneman introduces two hypothetical agents: System 1 and System 2. This model provides a framework for understanding how thought processes work. System 1 is responsible for fast thinking, it operates automatically, intuitively, and with little effort. System 2, on the other hand, governs slow thinking, it works analytically, consciously, and requires effort.

    Recent findings suggest that these two systems interact continuously whenever we are awake. System 1 runs constantly and automatically, while System 2 operates in an energy-saving mode, only stepping in occasionally. As a result, System 2 rarely takes control. Typically, System 2 adopts the impressions and intuitions generated by System 1 and accepts its intuitive responses.

    Recent findings suggest that the division of labor between the two systems is highly efficient. From an evolutionary perspective, this can be explained by the need to react rapidly to threats while also engaging in deliberate, long-term planning. Thus, the automatic System 1 developed primarily for threat detection, while the energy-intensive System 2 evolved to support complex reasoning, though it is less frequently engaged in full.

    According to recent reports, however, it is particularly System 1 that is susceptible to cognitive biases. Due to its energy efficiency, it is limited in logic and statistical reasoning. It often tends to substitute complex questions with simpler ones. System 2, in turn, tends to adopt these flawed outputs, as it does not always monitor or correct the conclusions generated by System 1.

    The following simple and intuitive thinking task illustrates the interplay between System 1 and System 2:.

    In a recent development, team A has 62% possession and wins a match 1-0. Team B has 38% possession and loses. Which team was more dominant?

    Of course, Team A was more dominant. At least, that’s the intuitive conclusion System 1 leads most people to. However, it neglects the fact that possession is not necessarily a reliable measure of dominance, and that match results are very imprecise indicators of performance. Despite lacking detailed data, System 1 assembles the question into a coherent picture. System 2 supports System 1’s incorrect solution, even though with minimal effort it could have reached the correct conclusion. However, System 2 is not consciously engaged.

    From this, it follows that people rely on mental shortcuts, so-called heuristics, to promptly solve complex problems. Heuristics are usually very helpful due to their efficiency but can sometimes lead to errors in judgment, known as biases. This is where the relevance for football analysis arises, as will be shown in the following section.

    “A heuristic is, technically defined, a simple procedure that helps us find adequate, though often imperfect, answers to difficult questions.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    First, I have linked a YouTube video that you should watch:.

    Industry observers note that even if you are already familiar with the video, its insights are remarkable. On the one hand, it can be concluded that focusing on one task can make us blind to other processes. To see and orient ourselves, we need a certain level of attention. However, the main insight of the video is that we cannot believe we have missed something so obvious. For those who did not see the gorilla, the player leaving the scene, or the curtain changing colors, it is unimaginable not to have noticed such obvious events.

    “We can be blind to the obvious, and we are also blind to our blindness.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    Sources indicate that applied to our football analysis, this once again demonstrates how prone we are to errors. How can we direct our attention to all levels of football tactics when, at the slightest distraction, we don’t even see a gorilla? We are only just beginning to discover many additional dimensions of the game as reference points, alongside spatial considerations in positional play. It is not only individual situations that are overlooked due to lack of attention, but possibly entire dimensions and we may not even be aware of this.

    It has been revealed that we only realize our mistakes when we can no longer analyze a team with the tools we have. We follow our own subjective beliefs in analysis and overlook other logical conclusions that could have been drawn equally well from the existing data. This problem becomes particularly interesting when assessing tactical risk.

    Sources indicate that recall the earlier question where you were asked to judge a team’s dominance based on possession percentages and the match result. System 1 constructed the best story it could from high possession and a win. What was not done, however, was likely questioning what is necessary to authentically assess a team’s dominance. We are blind to what we do not pay attention to.

    Sources indicate that hasty conclusions based on limited data form the basis of many heuristics. Kahneman refers to these conclusions as “What You See Is All There Is” (WYSIATI).

    “It is easier to fit everything you know into a coherent pattern when you know very little.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    This central mechanism explains why consistency of information, rather than its completeness, is what primarily shapes our beliefs. Unfortunately, we also interpret information accordingly through our coherence-seeking System 1. Kahneman explains that System 1 is completely insensitive to the quality and quantity of information from which impressions and intuitions arise. System 1 looks for coherent information, while a lazy System 2 fails to check it.

    “They did not want more information that might spoil their story. WYSIATI.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    To start, I have prepared a question that should first be answered:.

    How successful will Relationism be compared to Positionism in the next ten years in the top 5 leagues?

    The answer will follow at the end of this section….

    It has been revealed that to interpret actions and processes, a complex, multidimensional understanding of the game is necessary. In analysis, we face difficult questions that can be answered on multiple levels. Often, there is not just one correct analysis, but several possibilities which together create an accurate picture.

    In a recent development, “I know that I know nothing.” (cf. Plato, Apology 22d: “For I was conscious that I knew practically nothing…” ).

    According to recent reports, through reflection and the constant questioning of our observations and conclusions, we come closer to the goal of better understanding the game. The ability to accept that there are always newly introduced perspectives and interpretations fosters a deeper, more nuanced understanding. Unfortunately, when faced with complex matters, humans intuitively tend to fall into different patterns of thinking.

    Kahneman explains that even with complex questions, we rarely seem overwhelmed. We are able to provide answers to questions we do not fully understand. But why is that?

    Heuristics, as explained above, can be defined as mental shortcuts. Unfortunately, complex questions must also be answered in an energy-efficient way. Thus, we tend to substitute complex questions with simpler ones. This concept underlying many heuristics is called substitution. Often, we do not even notice that we have replaced a difficult question. However, we then use the answer to the simpler question to respond to the complex one. System 1 strives for the simplest possible answer to a question, while System 2, due to its inertia, does not verify the answer.

    “You are not overwhelmed, you don’t have to exert much effort, and you may not even notice that you have not answered the question that was asked of you.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    The concept of substitution is particularly pronounced when emotions are involved in the actual target question. Emotional attitudes amplify the effect. In the case of the so-called affect heuristic (judgments based on emotions), the interaction between System 1 and System 2 is especially prone to disruption. In the context of emotions and attitudes, System 2 does not act as a self-critic but rather as an advocate for the answer proposed by System 1. It looks for arguments that support its own beliefs.

    Let us return to the question posed at the beginning of this section. You most likely found an answer to how successful Relationismus will be in the future. However, instead of systematically thinking through the target question, an answer intuitively came to you that corresponds to your beliefs. The heuristic question you unconsciously answered might have been: How much do I like Guardiola’s Positionismus?

    It has been revealed that instead of searching for counterarguments against the intuitive answer, you subsequently searched for arguments that support your beliefs. To make a reliable future prediction, it would actually be necessary to free oneself from prejudices and break down the problem into its components, systematically questioning in which situations relational play is superior to positional play and in which situations the opposite is true. After all, the two philosophies can also be combined.

    It has been revealed that it can be concluded that substitution, together with WYSIATI, forms two of the most key mechanisms in the interplay of System 1 and System 2 underlying many systematic cognitive errors. The following section will introduce another mechanism: priming.

    Priming is a fundamental mechanism that explains how we process information when thinking. Our memory plays a central role in this, more precisely, the way it connects information. This principle is called association.

    Kahneman uses a metaphor to explain association: “Like ripples on the surface of a pond, activation spreads through a small part of the vast network of associated representations.” Even a single stimulus can be enough to unconsciously activate adjacent concepts or memories.

    Sources indicate that A priming effect occurs when a specific stimulus, a word, an image, a situation, etc. unconsciously activates certain content in memory. This automatic chain of activation influences how we think, feel, or act without us noticing. The brain essentially lays down mental pathways in the associative network, thereby facilitating the unconscious retrieval of information.

    To illustrate, here is a simple example: “If you have recently seen or heard the word eat, you will be temporarily more likely to complete the word fragment so_p as soup rather than soap. The opposite would happen if you had just seen the word wash.”– Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    Priming is already being used effectively in football contexts. For example, tactical training that includes video analysis and corresponding training formats represents a form of priming. By showing (tactical) videos during team meetings or recreating game-like patterns in training sessions, players can recognize familiar situations during matches, allowing them to react more promptly and effectively. Training decision-making under pressure and developing speed of action can therefore be linked to the priming effect.

    Another well-known example of this effect is the “Florida effect.” For those interested in reading more, I’ve linked the original 1996 study by John A. Bargh, Mark Chen, and Lara Burrows.

    Priming also plays a role in many other areas of football. It can be deliberately used to create positive outcomes, but it can also have unintended negative effects. Depending on the context, different types of priming are distinguished, such as semantic priming, affective priming, goal priming, and many more. In football, priming is also used, for example, in injury prevention and rehabilitation.

    Industry observers note that priming can also be used for the cognitive preparation of a match. In the so-called “Moments of Excellence,” players consciously recall their best past performances immediately before a game. Particularly interesting is the application of “success priming” by the coach, through the use of specific words or phrases in the pre-match talk. Attached is a 2006 study by Stajkovic, Locke, and Blair on this topic, specifically on the unconscious performance enhancement through goal activation.

    Analysts, too, are subject to unconscious priming. A glance at the final score before conducting an analysis primes their expectations and subtly shifts the approach toward explaining the outcome, even though the final score, due to its inaccuracy as a performance indicator, notes little about a team’s actual dominance.

    In a recent development, given the scope of the subject, an entire article could likely be written solely on the use of priming in football. In this article, however, the foundations of priming are used to understand it as one of the mechanisms underlying cognitive biases that affect football analysis.

    “They were primed to find flaws, and that is exactly what they found.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    Note: An earlier version mentioned the so-called “Florida Effect.” This belongs to a group of priming phenomena that, in the context of the replication crisis, have been only weakly or not at all confirmed. Those interested in learning more can find further information in the comment section. Many thanks to “AG” for the attentive feedback!

    Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the introduction, I explained that distortions in our thinking and decision-making occur in predictable ways under certain conditions. By now, you should have developed a basic understanding of how our thinking is governed by the interaction between System 1 and System 2, how intuitive judgments arise in the process of analysis, and how mechanisms such as WYSIATI, substitution, and priming can specifically contribute to systematic biases in football analysis.

    So far, around 200 cognitive biases have been identified. However, unlike many other articles that present a long list of biases with only brief descriptions, I deliberately refrain from doing so here. In my view, a simple enumeration does little to help recognize or avoid these distortions in practice. Instead, I focus on a small number of key biases that are particularly relevant to football analysis. Part 2 of this series will examine additional biases in the context of overconfidence.

    “Coherence means that you’re going to adopt one interpretation in general. Ambiguity tends to be suppressed. This is part of the mechanism that you have here that ideas activate other ideas and the more coherent they are, the more likely they are to activate to each other. Other things that don’t fit fall by the wayside. We’re enforcing coherent interpretation. We see the world as much more coherent than it is.” – Daniel Kahneman, Edge.

    What Kahneman describes here is the phenomenon called associative coherence. The processing of subjectively fitting information is facilitated by associative memory, while the processing of mismatching information is hindered. System 1 thus generates a coherent pattern of activated ideas in associative memory.

    This phenomenon inevitably leads to errors in analysis. We should be aware that our analysis alone will never capture the entirety of the subject being analyzed. The analysis is always an expression of the analyst’s beliefs and the ideas activated in their associative memory. Even though System 2 can counteract when activated, it is still influenced by System 1. The concept of associative coherence is therefore closely related to WYSIATI and priming.

    As part of the outcome of associative coherence, confirmation bias can be seen. It describes our tendency to want to confirm our existing beliefs.

    “The coherence of associative activation induces a confirmatory bias when people examine a hypothesis by increasing the accessibility of hypothesis-consistent information. For example, the intention to test the proposition that ‘Sam is friendly‘ preferentially activates evidence of Sam’s friendliness, whereas testing the proposition that ‘Sam is not friendly‘ preferentially evokes instances of hostile behavior.” – Associative Processes in Intuitive Judgement.

    According to recent reports, in analysis, we tend to seek out, select, and interpret information in a way that confirms our expectations. This, of course, applies to all areas of football analysis. Active countermeasures are necessary to avoid overlooking data that contradicts one’s own hypothesis.

    To simplify the illustration of anchoring, please answer the following two questions one after the other.

    Does Cristiano Ronaldo have more or less than 1,200 international matches for the senior national team?

    How many international matches for the senior national team has Cristiano Ronaldo played?

    It has been revealed that you have very likely come to the conclusion that Ronaldo has played fewer than 1,200 international matches. Nevertheless, this value probably influenced your estimate of the second question towards a number that is too high. Ronaldo has (as of March 2025) played 219 international matches.

    It has been revealed that judgments are often based on the first piece of information given, the anchor. This biases the estimate in its direction. Daniel Kahneman distinguishes two psychological mechanisms that explain this effect.

    The anchoring effect is measured and demonstrated in most psychological studies using numerical estimates, for example by estimating prices or probabilities. However, such quantitative judgments are not directly present in video analysis in football. To nevertheless apply the anchoring effect to this context, a change of perspective is useful: Richards J. Heuer Jr., among others a former CIA analyst, investigated the influence of cognitive biases, including the anchoring effect, on qualitative judgment processes within the intelligence community. In his book Psychology of Intelligence Analysis, Heuer deliberately does not refer only to mere numerical estimates, but to all kinds of ongoing judgments or assessments that an analyst inherits from predecessors or gradually revises themselves. Empirical evidence for the effectiveness of anchoring effects in sports video analysis is still lacking, but an analogy via the intelligence community is plausible.

    In a recent development, as already described above, the match result provides the analyst with the first available piece of information, acting as a kind of anchor. A 4–0 or 2–1 score leads us to attribute tactical superiority to the winning team and to base our tactical assessments too strongly on the result.

    “We should, in any case, assume that every number presented to us has an anchoring effect on us (…).” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    Another example of an anchoring effect in video analysis can be found when analyzing multiple matches of a team. The first game analyzed sets an initial assessment of the team’s tactical approach. As the analysis progresses, the analyst may need to revise their judgments but often fails to adjust sufficiently and remains primarily anchored to the initial assessment. This results in a biased analysis skewed toward the anchor game.

    „Even when analysts make their own initial judgment, and then attempt to revise this judgment on the basis of new information or further analysis, there is much evidence to suggest that they usually do not change the judgment enough.” – Psychology of Intelligence Analysis.

    It is not surprising that people look for reference points when faced with complex challenges, the anchor provides exactly this orientation. Unfortunately, in certain cases, it distorts our decision-making. Mussweiler and Strack investigated in their study “Overcoming the Inevitable Anchoring Effect: Considering the Opposite Compensates for Selective Accessibility” how the anchoring effect can be mitigated. Simply being aware of the anchor and the effect is unfortunately not enough to avoid the bias. Instead, a strategy of deliberately thinking about the opposite proves effective in preventing it. Imagine, instead of a 4–0 victory, a 0–4 defeat, and consider how your analysis would look in that case.

    Outcome Bias describes the tendency to judge performance based on the outcome. It is closely related to the principle of anchoring. The result serves as an anchor that shifts the judgment in its direction.

    Industry observers note that unlike the example mentioned above regarding bias from the match result, Outcome Bias can be applied to all types of results. This means that individual actions and sequences by players are evaluated based on their success or failure, regardless of the actual quality of execution.

    Sources indicate that an example of this is a successful pressing sequence that leads to winning the ball. Because of the positive outcome, the pressing is overall rated as good. However, other relevant factors, such as intensity, timing, the opponent’s reaction, etc. are either not considered at all or only insufficiently taken into account.

    If the same pressing sequence is executed again in a different game situation but fails to win the ball, the pressing is suddenly rated as poor, even though the execution was identical. This bias demonstrates how strongly the evaluation is influenced by the outcome rather than by the quality of the action itself. All actions in the game can be subject to Outcome Bias in analysis.

    According to recent reports, to prevent Outcome Bias, the evaluation criteria should be adjusted. Instead of judging a performance by its outcome, the process quality should be assessed. This increases the likelihood of future successful actions.

    The availability heuristic describes a cognitive shortcut in which people assess the frequency or likelihood of events based on how easily examples come to mind. In doing so, the original question: “How often does an event occur?” is replaced by a simpler one: “How easily can I recall relevant examples?”. This is a typical example of the substitution mechanism.

    In a recent development, more vital for the availability of an action than the number of examples one can recall is how easily they come to mind, what is known as ease of retrieval. A paradoxical example illustrating the effect of the availability heuristic was demonstrated by Schwarz et al. in 1991: people are less convinced by a decision when asked to list as many arguments in favor of it as possible. This approach plays the two factors, number of arguments and ease of retrieval, against each other: the more arguments that must be generated, the harder they are to retrieve.

    In the context of football analysis, this heuristic can lead to an overestimation of certain in-game actions or patterns, particularly during live matches. Striking, prominent, or emotional moments are more easily remembered and therefore disproportionately influence our overall evaluation of the game, regardless of how frequent or relevant they actually were. The availability heuristic has a particularly strong impact on our perception of risk (explored in Part 2).

    According to recent reports, the game scenes most readily accessible to the analyst are also heavily influenced by their subjective experiences. A wide range of impressions, such as those from previous roles, past matches, or preferred playing philosophies, shape which factors and thus which moments are emphasized in the analysis. A strong bias toward particular strategies, such as overloads in possession, can distort the analysis by neglecting other decisive elements like timing. This simply stems from the complexity and diversity inherent to football. In this way, personal experience encourages subjective conclusions through the combination of the availability heuristic and WYSIATI.

    The representativeness heuristic describes judgments about probability based on how representative something appears to be. Representativeness here refers to stereotypes and perceived similarity. When asked about probability, people often engage in substitution, evaluating plausibility instead of actual likelihood. Kahneman illustrates this with the following example:.

    “You see a person reading The Newly introduced York Times on the New York subway. Which of the following is a better bet about the reading stranger?

    She does not have a college degree.”.

    While the more plausible story might lead you to bet on the PhD, you should consider the base rates. Given that far more people without a college degree ride the Latest York subway than people with doctorates, the statistically sounder bet would be on the person not having a college degree. This example highlights the tension between base rate information and representativeness.

    “The representativeness heuristic is misleading when it causes people to ignore base rate information that points in a different direction.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    Recent findings suggest that kahneman accordingly advises questioning the informativeness of data and anchoring probability judgments to plausible base rates. To further illustrate the relevance of this concept in a football context, consider the following recent example:.

    At the beginning of the 2024/25 season, Bayern Munich employed an aggressive, man-marking high press. This tactical approach faced heavy criticism, primarily due to the potential for conceding counterattack goals. Despite the fact that several clubs, such as Atalanta Bergamo, had already been successfully using man-marking in high pressing for years on the international stage, the approach was viewed as atypical in Germany. Since the 1990s, man-marking had largely been replaced in the Bundesliga by zonal marking or hybrid forms. The evaluation of Bayern’s pressing was guided by historical prototypes of man-marking, particularly those involving a libero and, thus, a structural numerical inferiority. Although the man-marking was implemented in a completely different tactical fashion, the comparison seemed plausible due to the similarity and influenced judgments about its success.

    It has been revealed that in reality, the base rates painted a different picture: Bayern dominated their early Bundesliga matches, prevented opponents from gaining a foothold, and significantly limited their scoring opportunities. Statistically, the approach was highly successful: in their first 11 matches, 7 opponents failed to exceed an xG value of 0.5. The previous season’s champions, Leverkusen, only managed an xG of 0.17 and just 27% possession.

    In a recent development, nonetheless, the assessment of Bayern’s man-marking pressing was distorted by the representativeness heuristic: instead of evaluating the actual likelihood of success based on objective data, the plausibility of an outdated playing style was used as the basis of judgment. This illustrates how stereotypical mental models can lead to misjudgments and how crucial it is to critically examine information in football analysis.

    It has been revealed that for the sake of completeness, it should be mentioned that individual statistics (base rates in football) are not necessarily meaningful on their own. However, a combination of multiple statistics and data points can produce a more reliable picture to guide analysis. While xG values (as a combination of several data inputs) are still prone to error and need to be contextualized, they can nonetheless provide valuable insights into a team’s actual performance over time.

    In a recent development, the conjunction fallacy is one of the cognitive errors that arise from the representativeness heuristic. It describes the tendency of people to judge the combination of two events as more likely than one of the events alone, even when directly compared. The prerequisite is that the combination creates a more coherent and plausible story than the single event. One of the most controversial and well-known examples is the “Linda problem” by Kahneman and Tversky:.

    According to recent reports, “Linda is 31 years old, single, outspoken and very bright. She majored in philosophy. As a student, she was deeply concerned with problems of discrimination and social justice, and also participated in anti-nuclear demonstrations.

    Which of the following is more probable?

    Linda is a bank teller and is active in the feminist movement.”.

    Despite the intuitive plausibility that Linda’s characteristics align more closely with the feminist movement, the first option is statistically more probable. After all, the conjunction of two events (“Linda is a bank teller and is active in the feminist movement”) is always less likely than one of the events alone (“Linda is a bank teller”).

    „The most representative outcomes combine with the personality description to yield the most coherent stories. The most coherent stories are not necessarily the most probable, but they are plausible, and the concepts of coherence, plausibility, and probability are easily confused by the unwary.“ – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    The “less-is-more pattern” by Christopher Hsee ties into this problem. For those who want to read more, I’ve linked the relevant study here. It states that the probability of the broader event (e.g., Linda is a bank teller) must be higher than that of the event that is included within it (e.g., Linda is a bank teller and active in the feminist movement). However, the more plausible event (less comprehensive) is judged to be more probable than the less plausible, more comprehensive one. This creates the “less-is-more” pattern. As a result, the probability estimate for the more detailed scenario is higher, even though this contradicts logical reasoning.

    “This is the trap for forecasters and their clients: the more detailed the scenarios, the more convincing they are, but the less probable they become.” – Thinking, Fast and Slow.

    In a recent development, in the context of opponent team analysis for an upcoming match, the analyst must be aware that they are the forecaster, making probability estimates about the opponent’s future style of play. Thus, they should assess the likelihood of events, not merely their plausibility.

    Applying Hsee’s “less-is-more principle” to this context means that detailed, plausible match scenarios may sound impressive, but are statistically less reliable for prediction than broader descriptions. Each additional assumption in a forecast multiplies individual probabilities and thereby reduces the overall likelihood of an accurate prediction.

    However, this is not a call for a lack of detail in opponent analysis. On the contrary, the more detailed, precise, and comprehensive the analysis, the better the ability to derive general playing principles, patterns, and behaviors of the opponent. Therefore, the analyst should aim to analyze the opponent as holistically as possible before making generalized statements that increase the predictive probability.

    Sources indicate that while in Part 2 I will address structural conditions in football that affect the intuition of analyst and coach experts, in this section I will focus on the individual conditions of different types of analysis. Even though I speak here about football analysis in general, it is important to clarify that there are various forms of analysis in football (see table). Different types of analysis also have different individual susceptibilities to cognitive biases.

    According to recent reports, certain biases are additionally triggered by specific types of analysis. Prediction, for example, is particularly affected by the representativeness heuristic, since it involves assessing probabilities. Team analysis over multiple games increases susceptibility to the anchoring heuristic, and post-match analysis is prone to hindsight bias, the tendency to overestimate the predictability of an event after it has occurred.

    Industry observers note that similarly, focusing on a single level of analysis increases vulnerability to WYSIATI. You should now be familiar with the cognitive errors mentioned here, so they should not come as a surprise. One factor not yet addressed in this article, which demonstrably increases susceptibility to all biases, is time pressure. Time pressure plays a significant role especially during live analysis, though not exclusively.

    Time pressure forces analysts to make quicker decisions. Research indicates that under such conditions, people rely more heavily on heuristics, increasing the likelihood of errors. Among other studies, Finucane et al. (2000) examined the influence of the affect heuristic on the evaluation of benefits and risks, demonstrating that time pressure amplifies this effect.

    Sources indicate that analysts therefore have to rely more on their intuition during live analysis. This brings me to Part 2, where I will identify conditions that increase experts’ susceptibility to intuitive errors.

    Recent findings suggest that by now, it should be clear why we delve so deeply into the mechanisms of heuristics. Without a fundamental understanding of how they work, heuristics and cognitive biases are difficult to recognize.

    Many behavioral psychology insights can be profitably applied in sports analysis. This includes not only heuristics and cognitive biases but can also be extended to other areas of football analysis. However, to cover these application areas sufficiently, there will be a Part 2, Part 3, and, if necessary, a Part 4.

    According to recent reports, in Part 2, I will address the topic of overconfidence. Among other things, it will examine the susceptibility of expert intuition as well as risk strategies and risk assessments in football. Strategies for avoiding biases in football analysis will also be presented.

    Part 3 (and possibly Part 4) will focus on “noise” in football analysis. Unlike bias, noise does not describe the distortion of judgments in a particular direction but the unconscious variability of multiple judgments under identical decision conditions.

    Cubs signing NPB slugger Teruaki Sato on six-year, $120 million contract as offseason overhaul continues

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that not long after fortifying their rotation with the signing of Trevor Rogers, the Chicago Cubs struck again by landing slugger Teruaki Soto out of Japan.
    • In a recent development, earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Sato, who turns 28 in March, as the No.
    • Industry observers note that "He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that not long after fortifying their rotation with the signing of Trevor Rogers, the Chicago Cubs struck again by landing slugger Teruaki Soto out of Japan. The club announced the signing on Friday, and the contract is for $120 million over six years, ESPN reports.

    In a recent development, earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Sato, who turns 28 in March, as the No. 4 free agent of the current 2026-27 class. Here's part of our write-up:.

    Industry observers note that "He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact concerns to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.".

    Industry observers note that sato is expected to play a corner outfield spot for the Cubs even though he's a corner infielder by trade. He does, however, have significant time in the outfield, where the Cubs are in need of help after the incumbent corner outfielders, Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki, departed in free agency. In 2026, Suzuki and Happ combined for a WAR of 7.8, so the bar for Sato will be relatively high when it comes to replacing a chunk of that value.

    It has been revealed that in addition to the $120 million contract owed to Sato, the Cubs also must pay Sato's former team, the Hanshin Tigers, a posting fee. For contracts in excess of $50 million, the posting agreement between MLB and NPB mandates that the posting fee will be 20% of the first $25 million plus 17.5% of the next $25 million plus 15% of the total guaranteed value exceeding $50 million. In the Cubs' case, that comes to a bit more than $20 million they'll owe Hanshin.

    It has been revealed that the Cubs are coming off a 2026 season in which they won 89 games and earned a postseason berth as the second-place team in the National League Central. In the playoffs, though, they were swept out of the Wild Card Series by the San Diego Padres in two games.

    Industry News: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the newly introduced Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions.
    • “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City.
    • It has been revealed that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the newly introduced Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

    “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

    It has been revealed that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

    Industry observers note that as it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    Recent findings suggest that there was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

    “They know how to do it,” Arteta mentioned of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”.

    Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

    “Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they revealed it,” Lampard noted. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”.

    "They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard mentioned Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt.

    Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he mentioned, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

    If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

    It has been revealed that the energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment upcoming signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

    It has been revealed that the opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

    Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

    Recent findings suggest that saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    According to recent reports, odegaard demonstrated in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

    In a recent development, "It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx.

    From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

    "How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I.

    "I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE.

    It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

    Sources indicate that FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J.

    Sources indicate that there will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

    According to recent reports, awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

    Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

    Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

    Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

    Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

    Recent findings suggest that odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

    Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

    In a recent development, lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

    Industry observers note that here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

    Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

    The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

    Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his upcoming side.

    In a recent development, odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

    The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a substantial deflection and flies out for a corner.

    In a recent development, from a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

    Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

    Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

    According to recent reports, white overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

    Recent findings suggest that it's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6.

    According to recent reports, odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

    We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

    It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

    Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

    According to recent reports, once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

    There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

    The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

    Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

    Recent findings suggest that at the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

    In a recent development, coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

    Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

    Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

    Recent findings suggest that last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

    Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

    “The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”.

Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

    The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

    It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

    Sources indicate that as Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh glitch.

    Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

    🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA.

    To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

    The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

    Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta stated: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

    “Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”.

    Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

    Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy.

    Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

    In a recent development, the assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

    Meanwhile, Arteta has mentioned he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

    Recent findings suggest that “In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta noted. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”.

    Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

    “We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he remarked. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”.

    In a recent development, this is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that while Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani was once again one of the top performers in all of baseball this past season, he was not up to his recent standards.
    • Sources indicate that the wear and tear on the 32-year-old four-time MVP has led to some speculation that Ohtani's days as a two-way phenomenon might be numbered, especially since the same injuries that limited his pitching availability also probably compromised him at the plate.
    • "That's how I can best help the team, the role in which I can best put my strengths to use," Ohtani recently noted in Japanese, as translated by the California Post, about his usage as both a pitcher and the Dodgers' primary DH.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that while Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani was once again one of the top performers in all of baseball this past season, he was not up to his recent standards. His production at the plate slipped from the heights of his 2023-25 run, and on the mound, injuries to his right biceps and left knee limited him to just 85 ⅔ innings during the regular season and zero during his team's playoff run.

    Sources indicate that the wear and tear on the 32-year-old four-time MVP has led to some speculation that Ohtani's days as a two-way phenomenon might be numbered, especially since the same injuries that limited his pitching availability also probably compromised him at the plate. That, however, doesn't appear to be the case.

    "That's how I can best help the team, the role in which I can best put my strengths to use," Ohtani recently noted in Japanese, as translated by the California Post, about his usage as both a pitcher and the Dodgers' primary DH.

    According to recent reports, the expectation is that Ohtani will continue pitching in 2027, but, as ever, with an eye on having him energized and at or near peak when the postseason arrives. To hear Ohtani tell it, this means a careful workload, yes, but it doesn't necessarily mean an uncommonly light workload.

    "I think it's not good to not pitch enough," Ohtani said, "but that it's risky to pitch too much.".

    Even with the looming specter of an owner-implemented lockout that shuts down the sport and forbids contact between teams and rostered MLB players like Ohtani, this offseason may serve as a better foundation for Ohtani than last offseason did. That's because the 2025-26 offseason was complicated by preparation for the World Baseball Classic. As such, Ohtani figures to be able to adhere more closely to his typical winter routine this time around.

    Industry observers note that after the lockout ends and team-player lines of communication are reopened, Ohtani and the Dodgers will know more about his pitching plan for 2027. He's made just 14 starts in back-to-back seasons -- in 2025 his workload was limited as he returned from major elbow surgery -- and didn't pitch at all in 2024. Perhaps the hope is to find a way back to 2023, when he made 23 starts in his final season with the Los Angeles Angels.

    Whatever the specifics, the two-way show appears poised to go on until further notice, and that's good news for Ohtani, the Dodgers, and fans everywhere.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the Arizona Diamondbacks have acquired catcher and former No.
    • Davis, who was the first selection of the 2021 draft out of the University of Louisville, turned 27 in September.
    • Recent findings suggest that davis is arbitration-eligible this offseason and is under team control through the 2029 season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the Arizona Diamondbacks have acquired catcher and former No. 1 overall pick Henry Davis from the Pittsburgh Pirates in exchange for utility outfielder/infielder Tim Tawa, the teams announced.

    Davis, who was the first selection of the 2021 draft out of the University of Louisville, turned 27 in September. With the Pirates, he essentially functioned as ace Paul Skenes' personal catcher, catching 31 of Skenes' 32 starts in 2026 and making just 54 other starts behind the plate. Offensively, Davis has never adapted to the highest level. In 958 career plate appearances spread over parts of four MLB seasons, Davis has slashed .178/.265/.300, which comes to an OPS+ of just 55.

    Recent findings suggest that davis is arbitration-eligible this offseason and is under team control through the 2029 season. In Arizona, he figures to back up starter Gabriel Moreno, the two-time Gold Glove winner who finished sixth in the National League MVP vote in 2026.

    As for Tawa, who turns 28 in April, he has a career OPS+ of 84 over parts of two seasons at the highest level. He's spent time at every defensive position except for catcher and shortstop.

    The Pirates, at 82-80 last season, are coming off their first winning campaign since 2018. The Diamondbacks won 86 games but missed the playoffs for a third straight year.

    Now for some trade grades for this one.

    It's a trade for a backup catcher, so it is what it is. Maybe Davis, as, again, a former top pick, still has some unrealized upside, but he's not especially young. He was a consensus top-100 prospect in the minors, and as a minor-leaguer, Davis had a slash line of .290/.407/.529 in 827 plate appearances on the farm. At this point, it's not likely Davis is going to reach a vastly higher plane at the plate, but it's worth a swing given how limited his role figures to be in Arizona.

    Sources indicate that tawa is a right-handed-hitting utility sort who can steal a base on occasion but has never played shortstop. He'll be on Don Kelly's bench somewhere in the reserve pecking order between Jake Mangum and Jared Triolo.

    According to recent reports, he might get some run since Mangum and Triolo are both in line for occasional platoon-duty starts. Tawa might be vaguely useful, but cutting bait on Davis represents an organizational failure.

    The New York Knicks may have cut off contract extension talks with Karl-Anthony Towns before the season, but Towns is doing plenty of negotiating on his own behalf with his play. Towns has been extraordinary for a Knicks team that still hasn't found its top form after winning the title, but is trending that way with five straight wins to get to 11-6.

    According to recent reports, towns leads the league with 13.9 rebounds per game. It's not just his size; he is a technician on the glass with the way he gets into the body of his man to stop his forward momentum and then almost springs himself back toward the ball for a two-birds-with-one-stone maneuver.

    Meanwhile, Towns is averaging 21.8 of just about the most efficient points possible for a shooting substantial man at 54% overall and 41.5% on five 3s a game. His 15 straight double-doubles to start the season are a Knicks record. It's unlikely that he'll reach Bill Walton's all-time mark of 34 straight double-doubles to start the 1976-77 season, but with the way he's playing, you can't rule anything out.

    Sources indicate that towns now has 20 straight regular-season doubles dating back to last year, four times more than the next highest active streak (Victor Wembanyama presently has five straight). Towns gets to his 3s in every way. He pops. Stretches. His step-back is about the only thing not going for him at present, but it's a nasty weapon with how dangerous he is as a driver.

    It's tempting to think Towns should be firing off even more 3s, but he is so dialed in on his attack times and zones that it's best to just let him continue playing on balance. When Jalen Brunson is in, he steps back. When Brunson is out, he ramps up the scoring. He's become the best high-hub passer this side of Nikola Jokić; no dime is too ambitious for him, as he is into full anticipatory quarterbacking rather than waiting for things to show open, which marks the highest level of facilitation.

    Get it to Towns at the top and cut, and you've got a good chance for a bucket:.

    Watch here as the Knicks flank Towns with a pair of two-man screening actions on each side. The first one, on his right, doesn't yield anything. But like a quarterback, he keeps going through his progressions until a second source produces fruit.

    On a retrouvé le dilemme mortelle des Playoffs 2026 sur les actions autour de KAT le playmaker :Balle plein centre et deux jeux à deux de chaque côté.Ne switchez pas, et c'est un cut ouvert pour OG pic.twitter.com/TmIIB0yNfk.

    These cuts are open for the Knicks because Towns, first, has pulled the significant man away from the basket, and even more when Brunson is on the court and the defense has to be so concerned with the two-man handoffs that the lid is completely lifted.

    From there, Towns is a triple threat, weaponized as both a passer (four assists a game and almost six more potential assists), screener (55 screen assists), and of course as a driver when he sees the open lane.

    Notice how Towns doesn't just put the ball on the floor right away. He is so tuned into the off-ball movement. I know I keep using the quarterback analogy, but it's really what it is. He has the mobility to tuck the ball and run himself, but his first priority is more often to wait for his receivers to open up. His feel for when, where and how to attack has become surgical.

    The Knicks don't want to cross the second apron. Nobody does. They have to pay or lose Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek.     • It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, given those calamitous results, the future of Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has been called into question.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Dallas Cowboys suffered an embarrassing loss on Thanksgiving afternoon, blowing a 21-point lead against the division rival Philadelphia Eagles and backup quarterback Joe Milton — whom the Cowboys themselves cut at the end of training camp.

    Dallas is unfortunately no stranger to choking away games this season. The Thanksgiving upset was the Cowboys' second loss this season wherein they blew a multi-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter at home. It was also their second loss this season to a backup quarterback at home. Thursday evening's loss was the third game dropped on a game-losing field goal attempt either at the buzzer of regulation or in overtime, and the second of those three where their clock/game management decisions arguably cost them the win. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, the Cowboys have now posted the two highest win probabilities in a loss this season, with their 99.1% win probability against the Eagles topping their previous high of 98.3% in Week 8 against the Arizona Cardinals.

    It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, given those calamitous results, the future of Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has been called into question. There are only so many games you can blow, so many mistakes you can make before the calls for your job start coming. And for Schottenheimer, those calls have been coming for some time now.

    But Schottenheimer himself says he's unconcerned about the noise.

    It has been revealed that "I don't worry about that," Schottenheimer mentioned when asked about his job security, according to  The Athletic. "I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn't affect me.".

    It has been revealed that he might have good reason not to worry about speculation regarding his job security. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones goes out there every week and defends Schottenheimer to the masses, insisting Schottenheimer will lead the Cowboys to a Super Bowl and that he is not considering any coaching changes. Incredibly, Schottenheimer's job appears safe, at least for now.

    Schottenheimer did meet with both Jerry and Stephen Jones after the game to discuss the latest loss, but it sounds like the meeting was business as usual and pretty benign.

    "Our conversations were shared disappointment, but we're also ready to get back to work," he stated, per The Athletic.

    Sources indicate that the Cowboys have a whole lot of work to do. Whether that work ultimately leads to success is up for debate, and whether Schottenheimer should be in charge of directing it is another story entirely.

    Aberdeen  boss Mario Frick has vowed to go on the attack when his new-look team take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow night.

    Appointed as the club's new manager during the international break, Frick's reign got off to a flyer as Aberdeen won 4-2 away at Kilmarnock on Saturday.

    Renowned for a high-octane attacking style of play at his previous clubs, the 52-year-old Liechtensteiner has already generated a wave of positivity at Pittodrie.

    Aberdeen will face a tough task against an in-form Rangers side who are unbeaten in their last 13 matches.

    But Frick insists there is no prospect of his team turning up at Ibrox and parking the bus in their efforts to take a positive result.

    According to recent reports, 'I'm looking forward to it and I'm pretty confident in our squad,' he stated. 'Now we have to prove that and have another good performance.

    'That's not our style (to sit in and defend). We want to play like we did at Kilmarnock. That's our style of play.

    Frick is all smiles after his side put four goals past Kilmarnock in his first match in charge.

    According to recent reports, 'Rangers will be a tough game. They are very strong, especially at home. I saw a lot of quality, particularly in their forward areas.

    'We have to defend better than we did on Saturday, that's for sure, and that's what we're working on.

    'I have to get to know my players even better because it's only been a week since we arrived in Aberdeen, and that takes time.

    'But, of course, it helps when you win the first game. We've got some confidence now and I'm pretty confident we can take something from Ibrox.

    'At the weekend, you could see that the mentality is very good. We struggled during the first 20 minutes of the second half, but the substitutes were very good and had a huge impact.

    'I think, in the end, it was a deserved win and now we're looking forward to meeting Rangers at Ibrox.

    Industry observers note that 'Defensively, we have to improve. Otherwise, it will be very difficult. I'm pretty sure we can defend better.

    In a recent development, 'But, like I say, we want to play like we did at the weekend. It's not our style (just to sit back and defend).'.

    Kevin Nisbet is mobbed by team-mates after netting the first of his double at Rugby Park.

    After the doom and gloom of the Stephen Robinson era, Frick has immediately created a feelgood factor at Aberdeen.

    The fans were singing his name after the victory at Rugby Park on Saturday - and he wants to strengthen that feeling of unity throughout the club.

    In a recent development, 'It's been very good so far, especially with the win,' he added. 'The team has some confidence now and I see many players laughing.

    'That's very crucial because we do this for fun as well. When you go onto the pitch, you have to take things seriously, but always with enjoyment. That's very important.

    'The relationship between the team and the supporters is notable, not between the supporters and me, because the team is the most important thing.

    In a recent development, 'For the players' confidence, it was very crucial that so many supporters travelled to Kilmarnock and celebrated the win with us. That was the first step.

    Recent findings suggest that 'It's not the time for me to make a statement. It's the first time we're playing together at Ibrox, and it's key that we stick to our style of play.

    It has been revealed that 'That's the most crucial thing to me. It is an exciting game and we are looking forward to it.'.

    • It has been revealed that one of the most talented but also enigmatic free agents is heading to Toronto.
    • According to recent reports, chisholm is a year removed from a 31-homer, 31-steal, All-Star season with the New York Yankees, but his bat slipped badly in 2026, and he had his worst offensive season since his rookie year in 2021.
    • Industry observers note that we ranked Chisholm as the sixth-best free agent available this offseason, and the second-best position player.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that one of the most talented but also enigmatic free agents is heading to Toronto. The Blue Jays have agreed to a one-year contract with second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., reports ESPN. Fansided initially reported that the two sides were close. The deal is worth $20 million and includes a player option. In an interesting twist, the ESPN report notes that if Chisholm declines his player option, it converts to a $40 million team option.

    The Blue Jays have not yet confirmed the news.

    According to recent reports, chisholm is a year removed from a 31-homer, 31-steal, All-Star season with the New York Yankees, but his bat slipped badly in 2026, and he had his worst offensive season since his rookie year in 2021. He still managed 19 home runs and 41 stolen bases and has 30-30 upside, which the Blue Jays will surely hope to tap into next season.

    Industry observers note that we ranked Chisholm as the sixth-best free agent available this offseason, and the second-best position player. Here's the write-up:.

    In what was his worst season as a hitter since his rookie year in 2021, Chisholm was still a league-average bat in 2026, and his top-shelf defense and baserunning still landed him at 3.5 WAR. Chisholm is a style-over-substance player who is not for everyone, but his second base defense and near-MLB-best baserunning skills give him a very high floor. He's a reasonable bet for 20-ish home runs with the potential to go 30-30, and Chisholm has improved his plate discipline enough to run walk rates north of 10% the last two years. The downside is his propensity to swing and miss. Chisholm has posted below-average in-zone contact rates throughout his career and contact rates that low always come with risk. That risk is mitigated somewhat by the secondary skills (defense, etc.) and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29. You probably don't want him as your best or second-best player, but he's also an overqualified No. 6-7 hitter who brings so much else to the table.

    In a recent development, the Yankees declined to give Chisholm the $23.15 million qualifying offer, signaling a split was on the horizon. They will not gain a compensation draft pick for losing him, nor will the American League East rival Blue Jays surrender a draft pick for signing him.

    Recent findings suggest that with the Jays, Chisholm figures to slot into his preferred position of second base. Last season, Ernie Clement was Toronto's primary at the position, but he struggled at the plate with an OPS+ of just 78 for the season. Clement figures to return to a utility role for manager John Schneider. Chisholm also has experience at third base, but coming off a 33-homer campaign, Kazuma Okamoto figures to retain that role in Toronto for 2027.

    The Blue Jays claimed the pennant in 2025 and pushed the Los Angeles Dodgers to seven games in the World Series. Last season, however, they backslid to 83 losses and last place in the division. The offense was the key culprit for the Jays, and a rebound campaign for Chisholm would surely help matters. Not long ago, Toronto fortified the rotation with the free-agent addition of right-hander Kaima Taira out of Japan.
